sentences.zh: 【唐紀五十七】起屠維大淵獻二月，盡重光赤奮若六月，凡二年在奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 57] From the second month of the year Tuwé Dàyuānxiàn through the sixth month of Chongguāng Chìfèiruò; two years in all, with a fraction.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 57] From the second month of the year Tuwé Dàyuānxiàn through the sixth month of Chongguāng Chìfèiruò—two years and a fraction in all.

sentences.zh: 元和十四年（

translations.literal: The fourteenth year of Yuanhe (
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yuanhe (

sentences.zh: 己亥，公元八一九年）

translations.literal: jihai, corresponding to 819 CE)
translations.idiomatic: the year jihai, corresponding to 819 CE)

sentences.zh: 二月，李聽襲海州，克東海、朐山、懷仁等縣。

translations.literal: In the second month, Li Ting raided Haizhou and captured the counties of Donghai, Qushan, Huairen, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Li Ting struck at Haizhou and took Donghai, Qushan, Huairen, and the other counties there.

sentences.zh: 李愬敗平盧兵於沂州，拔丞縣。

translations.literal: Li Su defeated the Pinglu army at Yizhou and captured Cheng County.
translations.idiomatic: At Yizhou, Li Su routed the Pinglu forces and seized Cheng County.

sentences.zh: 李師道聞官軍侵逼，發民治鄆州城塹，修守備，役及婦人，民益懼且怨。

translations.literal: When Li Shidao heard that the imperial armies were pressing in, he conscripted the people to work on the moat of Yanzhou and strengthen its defenses; the labor extended even to women, and the populace grew ever more fearful and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that imperial troops were closing in, Li Shidao pressed the people into digging Yanzhou's moat and strengthening its defenses—even women were put to work—and fear and resentment spread through the city.

sentences.zh: 都知兵馬使劉悟，正臣之孫也，師道使之將兵萬餘人屯陽谷以拒官軍。

translations.literal: The commander of all military affairs, Liu Wu, was a grandson of Liu Zhengchen. Shidao had him lead more than ten thousand troops to camp at Yanggu and resist the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu, commander of all military affairs and grandson of Liu Zhengchen, was ordered by Shidao to hold Yanggu with more than ten thousand men against the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 悟務為寬惠，使士卒人人自便，軍中號曰劉父。

translations.literal: Wu strove to be lenient and generous, letting every soldier have his own ease; the army called him Father Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu made a point of treating his men generously and letting them have their way, and the troops nicknamed him Father Liu.

sentences.zh: 及田弘正渡河，悟軍無備，戰又數敗。

translations.literal: When Tian Hongzheng crossed the river, Wu's army was unprepared and suffered defeat after defeat in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Hongzheng crossed the river, Wu's troops were caught unprepared and lost battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 或謂師道曰：「劉悟不修軍法，專收眾心，恐有他志，宜早圖之。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Shidao, "Liu Wu does not enforce military discipline but devotes himself to winning the hearts of the troops; I fear he has other designs and should be dealt with early."
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned Shidao, "Liu Wu ignores military discipline and courts the men's loyalty—he may have other plans. You should move against him while you still can."

sentences.zh: 師道召悟計事，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Shidao summoned Wu to discuss affairs and intended to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao called Wu in to consult on affairs, planning to kill him.

sentences.zh: 或諫曰：「今官軍四合，悟無逆狀，用一人言殺之，諸將誰肯為用！

translations.literal: Someone remonstrated, "The imperial armies now surround us on all sides; Wu has shown no sign of rebellion. If you kill him on one man's word, which of the generals will still serve you willingly!
translations.idiomatic: Another adviser objected: "Imperial forces are closing in from every side, and Wu has given no sign of disloyalty. Kill him on one man's word, and who among the generals will still fight for you?

sentences.zh: 是自脫其爪牙也。」

translations.literal: You would be tearing out your own claws and fangs."
translations.idiomatic: You would only be tearing out your own claws and fangs."

sentences.zh: 師道留悟旬日，復遣之，厚贈金帛以安其意。

translations.literal: Shidao kept Wu for ten days, then sent him back with a lavish gift of gold and silk to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao detained Wu for ten days, then sent him back with generous gifts of gold and silk to put him at ease.

sentences.zh: 悟知之，還營，陰為之備。

translations.literal: Wu understood what was happening; on returning to camp he secretly made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Wu saw through the ploy; back in camp he quietly made ready.

sentences.zh: 師道以悟將兵在外，署悟子從諫門下別奏。

translations.literal: Because Wu was leading troops in the field, Shidao appointed Wu's son Congjian to the post of separate memorialist under the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: With Wu still in the field, Shidao appointed his son Congjian as a separate memorialist at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從諫與師道諸奴日遊戲，頗得其陰謀，密疏以白父。

translations.literal: Congjian spent his days in sport with Shidao's household slaves and learned much of their secret plots, which he reported to his father in confidential memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian spent his days carousing with Shidao's household staff and picked up much of their scheming, which he relayed to his father in secret reports.

sentences.zh: 又有謂師道者曰：「劉悟終為患，不如早除之。」

translations.literal: Again someone said to Shidao, "Liu Wu will be a trouble in the end; better to remove him early."
translations.idiomatic: Again someone urged Shidao, "Liu Wu will be trouble in the end—better cut him down now."

sentences.zh: 丙辰，師道潛遣二使繼帖授行營兵馬副使張暹，令斬悟首獻之，勒暹權領行營。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Shidao secretly sent two envoys with sealed orders in succession to Zhang Xuan, deputy commander of the expeditionary camp's military forces, ordering him to behead Wu and present his head, and compelling Xuan to take interim command of the camp.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Shidao secretly sent two envoys in succession with sealed orders to Zhang Xuan, deputy commander of the expeditionary forces, instructing him to cut off Wu's head and present it, and to assume interim command of the camp.

sentences.zh: 時悟方據高丘張幕置酒，去營二三里。

translations.literal: At the time Wu was on a high hill with an awning spread, feasting with wine, two or three li from camp.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was then feasting under an awning on a hilltop, two or three li from camp.

sentences.zh: 二使至營，密以貼授暹。

translations.literal: The two envoys reached the camp and secretly handed the sealed order to Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The two envoys reached camp and quietly handed the sealed order to Xuan.

sentences.zh: 暹素與悟善，陽與使者謀曰：「悟自使府還，頗為備，不可匆匆，暹請先往白之，云：『司空遣使存問將士，兼有賜物，請都頭速歸，同受傳語。』

translations.literal: Xuan had long been on good terms with Wu; he pretended to plot with the envoys and said, "Since Wu returned from the commissionerate he has been well on guard; we cannot act in haste. Let Xuan go first to inform him, saying, 'The Commissioner has sent envoys to inquire after the troops and also has gifts; please return at once, Commander, to receive the message together.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had always been friendly with Wu; he feigned agreement with the envoys and said, "Wu has been on his guard ever since he came back from headquarters—we cannot rush this. Let me go ahead and tell him that the Commissioner has sent envoys to inquire after the men and bring gifts, and ask the commander to return at once to hear the message with us.

sentences.zh: 如此，則彼不疑，乃可圖也。」

translations.literal: In this way he will not suspect us, and then we can carry out the plan."
translations.idiomatic: That way he will not suspect anything, and we can strike."

sentences.zh: 使者然之。

translations.literal: The envoys agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys agreed.

sentences.zh: 暹懷帖走詣悟，屏人示之。

translations.literal: Xuan hid the order in his bosom and ran to Wu; dismissing attendants, he showed it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan hid the order in his robe, ran to Wu, dismissed everyone else, and showed it to him.

sentences.zh: 悟潛遣人先執二使，殺之。

translations.literal: Wu secretly sent men ahead to seize the two envoys and kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu secretly sent men ahead to seize and kill the two envoys.

sentences.zh: 時已向暮，悟按轡徐行還營，坐帳下，嚴兵自衛。

translations.literal: Evening was falling; Wu held his reins and returned slowly to camp, sat beneath his tent, and kept his troops on strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk was falling; Wu rode slowly back to camp, took his seat in the tent, and posted a heavy guard.

sentences.zh: 召諸將，厲色謂之曰：「悟與公等不顧死亡以抗官軍，誠無負於司空。

translations.literal: He summoned the generals and said sternly, "Wu and you gentlemen have faced death without flinching to resist the imperial army; we have truly done no wrong by the Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the generals and said harshly, "You and I have risked death to hold off the imperial army—we have done the Commissioner no wrong.

sentences.zh: 今司空信讒言，來取悟首。

translations.literal: Now the Commissioner believes slander and has sent men to take Wu's head.
translations.idiomatic: Now he believes slander and has sent men to take my head.

sentences.zh: 悟死，諸公其次矣。

translations.literal: When Wu dies, you gentlemen will be next.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, you will be next.

sentences.zh: 且天子所欲誅者獨司空一人。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Son of Heaven wishes to punish only the Commissioner alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven wants only the Commissioner punished.

sentences.zh: 今軍勢日蹙，吾曹何為隨之族滅！

translations.literal: Our military position grows tighter by the day—why should we follow him to extermination of our clans!
translations.idiomatic: Our position grows worse every day—why follow him to the destruction of our families!

sentences.zh: 欲與諸公卷旗束甲，還入鄆州，奉行天子之命，豈徒免危亡，富貴可圖也。

translations.literal: I wish to join you in furling our banners, buckling on our armor, and returning to Yanzhou to carry out the Son of Heaven's command—not only to escape ruin, but wealth and honor may be won as well.
translations.idiomatic: I propose we furl our banners, arm ourselves, and march back into Yanzhou to obey the Son of Heaven—not merely to escape ruin, but to win wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: 諸公以為何如？」

translations.literal: What do you gentlemen think of this?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you say?"

sentences.zh: 兵馬使趙垂棘立於眾首，良久，對曰：「如此，事果濟否？」

translations.literal: The military commissioner Zhao Chuiji stood at the head of the assembly; after a long pause he replied, "If we do this, can the affair really succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Military commissioner Zhao Chuiji stood at the front of the crowd; after a long silence he asked, "Can this really succeed?"

sentences.zh: 悟應聲罵曰：「汝與司空合謀邪！」

translations.literal: Wu answered with a shout of abuse: "Are you in league with the Commissioner!"
translations.idiomatic: Wu roared back, "Are you in league with the Commissioner!"

sentences.zh: 立斬之。

translations.literal: He had him beheaded on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: He had him beheaded at once.

sentences.zh: 遍問其次，有遲疑未言者，悉斬之，並斬軍中素為眾所惡者，凡三十餘，屍於帳前。

translations.literal: He went through the rest one by one; any who hesitated or did not speak were all beheaded, together with those in the army whom the troops had long hated—more than thirty in all—their corpses before the tent.
translations.idiomatic: He went down the line; anyone who hesitated or held back was killed, along with men the troops had long hated—more than thirty in all—until corpses lay piled before the tent.

sentences.zh: 餘皆股粟，曰：「惟都頭命，願盡死！」

translations.literal: The rest trembled in their thighs and said, "We obey the Commander alone and are willing to die to the last man!"
translations.idiomatic: The rest shook with fear and cried, "We obey the commander—command us and we will die!"

sentences.zh: 乃令士卒曰：「入鄆，人賞錢百緡，惟不得近軍帑。

translations.literal: He then told the soldiers, "On entering Yanzhou, each man shall receive a reward of one hundred strings of cash, but none may approach the military treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He told the men, "When we enter Yanzhou, each of you gets a hundred strings of cash—but stay away from the military treasury.

sentences.zh: 其使宅及逆黨家財，任自掠取，有仇者報之。」

translations.literal: As for the commissioner's residence and the property of the rebel faction, you may plunder as you please; those with grudges may settle them."
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner's mansion and the rebels' households are yours to plunder, and anyone with a score to settle may do so."

sentences.zh: 使士卒皆飽食執兵，夜半聽鼓三聲絕即行，人銜枚，馬縛口，遇行人，執留之，人無知者。

translations.literal: He had the soldiers eat their fill and take up arms; at midnight, when the third watch of drums ended, they set out—men with gag-sticks in their mouths, horses with muzzles tied; anyone they met was seized and held, and no one knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: The men ate their fill and took up arms; at midnight, when the third drum roll ended, they marched—gag-sticks in their mouths, horses' muzzles bound; anyone they met was seized, and no one knew they were coming.

sentences.zh: 距城數里，天未明，悟駐軍，使聽城上柝聲絕，使十人前行，宣言「劉都頭奉帖追入城。」

translations.literal: A few li from the city, before dawn, Wu halted the army and waited until the night-watch clappers on the walls ceased; he sent ten men ahead to announce, "Commander Liu, acting on sealed orders, is pressing into the city."
translations.idiomatic: A few li from the city, before dawn, Wu halted and waited until the night watch on the walls fell silent; then he sent ten men ahead to announce that Commander Liu was entering the city on sealed orders."

sentences.zh: 門者請俟寫簡白使，十人拔刃擬之，皆竄匿。

translations.literal: The gatekeepers asked to wait while they wrote a note to inform the commissioner; the ten drew their blades and threatened them, and all fled and hid.
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeepers asked to write a note to the commissioner first; the ten drew their blades, and the guards scattered.

sentences.zh: 悟引大軍繼至，城中噪嘩動地。

translations.literal: Wu led the main force up behind them; uproar in the city shook the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Wu brought up the main force behind them, and uproar shook the city.

sentences.zh: 比至，子城已洞開，惟牙城拒守，尋縱火，斧其門而入。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, the outer city stood wide open; only the inner citadel held out. Soon they set fire and hacked through its gate to enter.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, the outer city was wide open; only the inner citadel still resisted. They set fire and hacked through its gate.

sentences.zh: 牙中兵不過數百，始猶有發弓矢者，俄知力不支，皆投於地。

translations.literal: The troops in the citadel numbered no more than a few hundred; at first some still shot arrows, but soon seeing they could not hold, all cast their weapons to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The citadel held only a few hundred men; a few still loosed arrows at first, but seeing they could not hold, they threw down their weapons.

sentences.zh: 悟勒兵升聽事，使捕索師道。

translations.literal: Wu drove his troops up to the audience hall and sent men to search for Shidao.
translations.idiomatic: Wu led his troops up to the audience hall and sent men to seize Shidao.

sentences.zh: 師道與二子伏廁床下，索得之，悟命置牙門外隙地，使人謂曰：「悟奉密詔送司空歸闕，然司空亦何顏復見天子！」

translations.literal: Shidao and his two sons hid beneath the privy couch; they were found and seized. Wu ordered them placed in an open space outside the inner gate and had someone say to him, "Wu, acting on a secret edict, is sending the Commissioner back to the capital—but what face has the Commissioner to see the Son of Heaven again!"
translations.idiomatic: Shidao and his two sons were found hiding under a privy bench. Wu had them placed in the open ground outside the inner gate and sent word: "I am sending you back to the capital on a secret edict—but what face do you have left to show the Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 師道猶有幸生之意，其子弘方仰曰：「事已至此，速死為幸！」

translations.literal: Shidao still harbored hope of living; his son Hongfang looked up and said, "Things have come to this—a swift death is our fortune!"
translations.idiomatic: Shidao still hoped to live; his son Hongfang looked up and said, "It has come to this—a quick death is the best we can hope for!"

sentences.zh: 尋皆斬之。

translations.literal: Soon all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all three were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 自卯至午，悟乃命兩都虞候巡坊市，禁掠者，即時皆定。

translations.literal: From the hour mao to the hour wu, Wu then ordered the two chief military inspectors to patrol the wards and markets and forbid looting; order was restored at once.
translations.idiomatic: From morning through midday Wu sent the two chief military inspectors to patrol the streets and forbid looting, and the city settled at once.

sentences.zh: 大集兵民於球場，親乘馬巡繞，慰安之。

translations.literal: He gathered soldiers and civilians in great numbers at the ball ground, mounted a horse himself to ride around them, and comforted and reassured them.
translations.idiomatic: He assembled soldiers and civilians on the drill ground, rode among them in person, and reassured them.

sentences.zh: 斬贊師道逆謀者二十餘家，文武將吏且懼且喜，皆入賀。

translations.literal: He beheaded more than twenty households that had praised Shidao's rebellion; civil and military officers were both fearful and pleased and all came in to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: He executed more than twenty households that had supported Shidao's rebellion; the civil and military staff came in both fear and relief to congratulate him.

sentences.zh: 悟見李公度，執手歔欷；

translations.literal: When Wu saw Li Gongdu he took his hand and wept;
translations.idiomatic: When Wu saw Li Gongdu he took his hand and wept;

sentences.zh: 出賈直言於獄，置之幕府。

translations.literal: he released Jia Zhiyan from prison and placed him on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: he released Jia Zhiyan from prison and took him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 悟之自陽谷還兵趨鄆也，潛使人以其謀告田弘正曰：「事成，當舉烽相白。

translations.literal: When Wu was leading his troops back from Yanggu toward Yanzhou, he had secretly sent someone to inform Tian Hongzheng of his plan, saying, "When the affair succeeds, I shall raise beacon fires to signal you.
translations.idiomatic: As Wu marched back from Yanggu toward Yanzhou, he had secretly told Tian Hongzheng of his plan: "When it succeeds, I will light beacon fires to let you know.

sentences.zh: 萬一城中有備不能入，願公引兵為助。

translations.literal: If by chance the city is prepared and we cannot enter, I ask that you lead troops to assist.
translations.idiomatic: If the city is prepared and we cannot get in, I ask you to bring your troops to help.

sentences.zh: 功成之日，皆歸於公，悟何敢有之！」

translations.literal: On the day success is achieved, all shall belong to you—how would Wu dare claim any of it!"
translations.idiomatic: When the day comes, everything is yours—I would not dare claim a thing!"

sentences.zh: 且使弘正進據己營。

translations.literal: He also had Hongzheng advance and occupy his own camp.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Hongzheng advance and occupy his camp.

sentences.zh: 弘正見烽，知得城，遣使往賀。

translations.literal: Hongzheng saw the beacons, knew the city had been taken, and sent envoys to congratulate him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng saw the beacons, knew the city had fallen, and sent envoys to congratulate him.

sentences.zh: 悟函師道父子三首遣使送弘正營，弘正大喜，露布以聞。

translations.literal: Wu boxed the three heads of Shidao and his sons and sent them by envoy to Hongzheng's camp; Hongzheng was greatly pleased and issued a public bulletin to report the news.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent Shidao and his two sons' heads in a box to Hongzheng's camp; Hongzheng was overjoyed and issued a public bulletin to the court.

sentences.zh: 淄、青等十二州皆平。

translations.literal: The twelve prefectures of Zi, Qing, and the rest were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: All twelve prefectures of Zi, Qing, and the rest were pacified.

sentences.zh: 弘正初得師道首，疑其非真，召夏侯澄使識之。

translations.literal: When Hongzheng first received Shidao's head he doubted it was genuine and summoned Xiahou Cheng to identify it.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzheng first received Shidao's head he doubted it was real and called in Xiahou Cheng to identify it.

sentences.zh: 澄熟視其面，長號隕絕者久之，乃抱其首，舐其目中塵垢，復慟哭。

translations.literal: Cheng looked closely at the face, wailed at length and fainted for a long time, then embraced the head, licked the dust from its eyes, and wept again in anguish.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng studied the face, wailed until he fainted, then embraced the head, licked the dust from its eyes, and wept again.

sentences.zh: 弘正為之改容，義而不責。

translations.literal: Hongzheng changed expression at this, honoring his loyalty and not blaming him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng's expression changed; he honored Cheng's loyalty and did not reproach him.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，田弘正捷奏至。

translations.literal: On renxu, Tian Hongzheng's report of victory arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Tian Hongzheng's victory report reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，命戶部侍郎楊於陵為淄青宣撫使。

translations.literal: On yichou, Yang Yuling, vice minister of revenue, was appointed commissioner to pacify and console Zi and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Vice Minister of Revenue Yang Yuling was appointed pacification commissioner for Zi and Qing.

sentences.zh: 己巳，李師道首函至。

translations.literal: On jisi, Li Shidao's head in a box arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Li Shidao's head arrived at the capital in a box.

sentences.zh: 自廣德以來，垂六十年，籓鎮跋扈河南、北三十餘州，自除官吏，不供貢賦，至是盡遵朝廷約束。

translations.literal: Since the Guangde era, nearly sixty years had passed in which the military commissioners had been overbearing in more than thirty prefectures north and south of the Yellow River, appointing their own officials and not submitting tribute and taxes; now all obeyed the court's constraints.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly sixty years since the Guangde era, more than thirty prefectures north and south of the Yellow River had lived under arrogant military commissioners who appointed their own officials and withheld tribute; now all submitted to the court's authority.

sentences.zh: 上命楊於陵分李師道地，於陵按圖籍，視土地遠邇，計士馬眾寡，校倉庫虛實，分為三道，使之適均：以鄆、曹、濮為一道，淄、清、齊、登、萊為一道，兗、海、沂、密為一道，上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yang Yuling to divide Li Shidao's territory. Yuling consulted the registers, considered the distance of lands near and far, reckoned the numbers of troops and horses, and compared the fullness or emptiness of storehouses, dividing the region into three circuits so that they would be suitably balanced: Yan, Cao, and Pu as one circuit; Zi, Qing, Qi, Deng, and Lai as another; Yan, Hai, Yi, and Mi as a third. The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yang Yuling to partition Li Shidao's domain. Yuling studied the registers, weighed distances, troop strengths, and storehouse stocks, and divided the territory into three balanced circuits: Yan, Cao, and Pu; Zi, Qing, Qi, Deng, and Lai; and Yan, Hai, Yi, and Mi. The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 劉悟以初討李師道詔云：「部將有能殺師道以眾降者，師道官爵悉以與之。」

translations.literal: Liu Wu, recalling the initial edict to campaign against Li Shidao, which said, "Any subordinate general who can kill Shidao and surrender with his forces shall receive all of Shidao's offices and ranks,"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu recalled the original edict against Li Shidao: "Any subordinate who kills Shidao and surrenders with his troops shall receive all of Shidao's offices and ranks."

sentences.zh: 意謂盡得十二州之地，遂補署文武將佐，更易州縣長吏；

translations.literal: understood this to mean he would gain all twelve prefectures in full; he therefore filled civil and military posts and replaced prefectural and county chiefs;
translations.idiomatic: He believed this meant all twelve prefectures were his; he appointed civil and military officers and replaced prefectural and county chiefs;

sentences.zh: 謂其下曰：「軍府之政，一切循舊。

translations.literal: and told his subordinates, "Military government affairs shall all follow the old ways.
translations.idiomatic: and told his men, "Army administration will go on as before.

sentences.zh: 自今但與諸公抱子弄孫，夫復何憂！」

translations.literal: From now on you need only hold your children and play with your grandchildren—what more is there to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: From now on we need only hold our grandchildren—what is left to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 上欲移悟他鎮，恐悟不受代，復須用兵，密詔田弘正察之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to transfer Wu to another command but feared Wu would not accept being replaced and troops would have to be used again; he secretly instructed Tian Hongzheng to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to move Wu to another post but feared he would not accept replacement and force another campaign; he secretly told Tian Hongzheng to watch him.

sentences.zh: 弘正日遣使者詣悟，託言修好，實觀其所為。

translations.literal: Hongzheng sent envoys to Wu every day, ostensibly to cultivate good relations but in fact to observe his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng sent envoys to Wu daily on the pretext of friendship, but in fact to watch what he did.

sentences.zh: 悟多力，好手搏，得鄆州三日，則教軍中壯士手搏，與魏博使者庭觀之，自搖肩攘臂，離坐以助其勢。

translations.literal: Wu was very strong and fond of hand-to-hand wrestling; three days after taking Yanzhou he had the army's stalwarts wrestle in the courtyard for the Weibo envoys to watch, himself rolling his shoulders and flexing his arms, rising from his seat to urge them on.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was powerfully built and loved wrestling; three days after taking Yanzhou he had his strongest men wrestle in the courtyard for the Weibo envoys, rolling his shoulders and leaving his seat to cheer them on.

sentences.zh: 弘正聞之，笑曰：「是聞除改，登即行矣，何能為哉！」

translations.literal: When Hongzheng heard of this he laughed and said, "When this man hears of his transfer he will set out at once—what can he do!"
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzheng heard this he laughed and said, "The moment he hears of his transfer he will leave—what trouble can he make?"

sentences.zh: 庚午，以悟為義成節度使。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Wu was appointed military commissioner of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Wu was appointed military commissioner of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 悟聞制下，手足失墜。

translations.literal: When Wu heard the appointment issued, his hands and feet lost their hold.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu heard the appointment, his limbs went slack with shock.

sentences.zh: 明日，遂行。

translations.literal: The next day he set out.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he departed.

sentences.zh: 弘正已將數道兵，比至城西二里，與悟相見於客亭，即受旌節，馳詣滑州，辟李公度、李存、郭昈、賈直言以自隨。

translations.literal: Hongzheng had already led troops from several circuits; when he reached a point two li west of the city he met Wu at a roadside pavilion; Wu at once received the insignia of command and galloped to Huazhou, taking Li Gongdu, Li Cun, Guo Han, and Jia Zhiyan on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng had already advanced with troops from several circuits; two li west of the city he met Wu at a roadside pavilion. Wu took the insignia of command at once and rode hard for Huazhou, taking Li Gongdu, Li Cun, Guo Han, and Jia Zhiyan with him.

sentences.zh: 悟素與李文會善，既得鄆州，使召之，未至。

translations.literal: Wu had long been on good terms with Li Wenhui; once he held Yanzhou he sent for him, but Wenhui had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Wu had long been friendly with Li Wenhui; after taking Yanzhou he sent for him, but Wenhui had not yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 聞將移鎮，昈、存謀曰：「文會佞人，敗亂淄青一道，滅李司空之族，萬人所共仇也！

translations.literal: When they heard Wu was to be transferred, Han and Cun plotted together and said, "Wenhui is a flatterer who ruined and threw into chaos the whole Zi-Qing circuit and exterminated Commissioner Li's clan—he is the common enemy of ten thousand men!
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Wu was to be transferred, Guo Han and Li Cun plotted: "Wenhui is a sycophant who wrecked Zi-Qing, destroyed Commissioner Li's family, and is hated by everyone!

sentences.zh: 不乘此際誅之，田相公至，務施寬大，將何以雪三齊之憤怨乎！」

translations.literal: If we do not take this chance to execute him, when Commissioner Tian arrives and devotes himself to leniency, how will the grievances of the Three Qi be avenged!"
translations.idiomatic: If we do not kill him now, when Commissioner Tian comes and shows mercy, how will the Three Qi ever have their revenge!"

sentences.zh: 乃詐為悟帖，遣使即文會所至，取其首以來。

translations.literal: They forged an order in Wu's name and sent an envoy to wherever Wenhui was to take his head and bring it back.
translations.idiomatic: They forged an order in Wu's name and sent men to wherever Wenhui was to bring back his head.

sentences.zh: 使者遇文會於豐齊驛，斬之。

translations.literal: The envoy met Wenhui at Fengqi Post Station and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy met Wenhui at Fengqi Post and killed him.

sentences.zh: 比還，悟及昈、存已去，無所覆命矣。

translations.literal: By the time they returned, Wu and Han and Cun had already left; there was no one to report to.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they returned, Wu, Guo Han, and Li Cun were gone; there was no one left to report to.

sentences.zh: 文會二子，一亡去，一死於獄，家貲悉為人所掠，田宅沒官。

translations.literal: Of Wenhui's two sons, one fled and one died in prison; the family wealth was all plundered by others and the fields and houses confiscated by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhui's two sons—one fled, one died in prison—and looters took everything; his lands and house were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 詔以淄青行營副使張暹為戎州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhang Xuan, deputy commander of the Zi-Qing expeditionary camp, prefect of Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Zhang Xuan, deputy commander of the Zi-Qing expedition, prefect of Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，加田弘正檢校司徒、同平章事。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Tian Hongzheng was promoted to honorary Grand Mentor and made co–Grand Councilor of State.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Tian Hongzheng was made honorary Grand Mentor and co–Grand Councilor of State.

sentences.zh: 先是，李師道將敗數月，聞風動鳥飛，皆疑有變，禁鄆人親識宴聚及道路偶語，犯者有刑。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the months before Li Shidao's defeat, at the sound of wind or the flight of birds he suspected trouble; he forbade the people of Yanzhou to gather with kin and friends for feasts or to converse casually on the roads, and offenders were punished.
translations.idiomatic: For months before his fall, Li Shidao suspected treachery at every rustle of wind or flight of birds; he banned gatherings among kin and friends and casual talk in the streets, punishing offenders.

sentences.zh: 弘正既入鄆，悉除苛禁，縱人遊樂，寒食七晝夜不禁行人。

translations.literal: Once Hongzheng entered Yanzhou he abolished all harsh prohibitions and let the people enjoy themselves freely; for seven days and nights around Cold Food Festival travelers were not restricted.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hongzheng entered Yanzhou he lifted every harsh restriction and let people enjoy themselves; for seven days and nights around Cold Food Festival no curfew was imposed.

sentences.zh: 或諫曰：「鄆人久為寇敵，今雖平，人心未安，不可不備。」

translations.literal: Someone remonstrated, "The people of Yanzhou have long been our enemies; though pacified now, hearts are not yet settled—you cannot fail to take precautions."
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged caution: "The people of Yanzhou were our enemies for years; though the city is pacified, hearts are unsettled—we must stay on guard."

sentences.zh: 弘正曰：「今為暴者既除，宜施以寬惠，若復為嚴察，是以桀易桀也，庸何愈焉！」

translations.literal: Hongzheng said, "Those who committed violence have now been removed; leniency and kindness should be shown. If we impose strict surveillance again, we would only be replacing one tyrant with another—how would that be any improvement!"
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng replied, "The violent are gone; this is the time for mercy. Strict surveillance again would only replace one tyrant with another—what would we gain?"

sentences.zh: 先是，賊數遣人入關，截陵戟，焚倉場，流矢飛書，以震駭京師，沮撓官軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, the rebels had repeatedly sent men into the passes to cut down the ceremonial halberds at the imperial tombs, burn the granaries and depots, and shoot arrows bearing letters to terrify the capital and thwart the imperial armies.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the rebels had repeatedly sent agents through the passes to cut down tomb halberds, burn storehouses, and shoot in letters meant to terrify the capital and hamper the imperial armies.

sentences.zh: 有司督察甚嚴，潼關吏至發人囊篋以索之，然終不能絕。

translations.literal: The authorities supervised very strictly; Tong Pass guards even opened people's bags and cases to search them, yet they could never stop it entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Official supervision was severe—Tong Pass guards even searched travelers' bags—but the agents could never be stopped entirely.

sentences.zh: 及田弘正入鄆，閱李師道簿書，有賞殺武元衡人王士元等及賞潼關、蒲津吏卒案，乃知向者皆吏卒賂於賊，容其奸也。

translations.literal: When Tian Hongzheng entered Yanzhou he examined Li Shidao's account books; there were records rewarding Wang Shiyuan and others for killing Wu Yuanheng, and cases rewarding clerks and soldiers at Tong Pass and Pujin Ferry—thus he learned that the agents who had entered the passes were all clerks and soldiers bribed by the rebels, who had sheltered their treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Once Tian Hongzheng entered Yanzhou he went through Li Shidao's ledgers and found rewards for Wang Shiyuan and others who had killed Wu Yuanheng, and for clerks and soldiers at Tong Pass and Pujin Ferry—proof that the men slipping through the passes had been bribed to let the rebels' agents through.

sentences.zh: 裴度纂述蔡、鄆用兵以來上之憂勤機略，因侍宴獻之，請內印出付史官。

translations.literal: Pei Du compiled an account of the emperor's anxious diligence and strategic planning since the campaigns in Cai and Yan, and at a banquet presented it, asking that an inner seal be applied so it could be released to the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du compiled a record of the emperor's anxious planning since the Cai and Yan campaigns and presented it at a banquet, asking that the palace seal be applied so it could go to the historiographers.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「如此，似出朕志，非所欲也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "In this way it would seem to express my own intent, which is not what I desire."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That would make it look as if it came from my own mind, which is not what I want."

sentences.zh: 弗許。

translations.literal: He did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊子，以華州刺史馬總為鄆、曹、濮等州節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wuzi, Ma Zong, prefect of Huazhou, was appointed military commissioner of Yan, Cao, Pu, and the other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuzi, Ma Zong, governor of Huazhou, was made military commissioner of Yan, Cao, Pu, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以義成節度使薛平為平盧節度、淄、青、齊、登、萊等州觀察使。

translations.literal: On jichou, Xue Ping, military commissioner of Yicheng, was appointed military commissioner of Pinglu and observation commissioner of Zi, Qing, Qi, Deng, Lai, and the other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Xue Ping of Yicheng was made military commissioner of Pinglu and observation commissioner over Zi, Qing, Qi, Deng, Lai, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 以淄青四面行營供軍使王遂為沂、海、兗、密等州觀察使。

translations.literal: Wang Sui, supply officer of the four-sided Zi-Qing expeditionary camp, was appointed observation commissioner of Yi, Hai, Yan, Mi, and the other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui, supply officer of the Zi-Qing expedition, was made observation commissioner of Yi, Hai, Yan, Mi, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 橫海節度使烏重胤奏：「河朔籓鎮所以能旅拒朝命六十餘年者，由諸州縣各置鎮將領事，收刺史、縣令之權，自作威福。

translations.literal: Wu Chongyin, military commissioner of Heng-hai, memorialized: "The reason the Hebei military commissioners could collectively defy the court's commands for more than sixty years was that each prefecture and county set up garrison generals to handle affairs, seizing the authority of prefects and magistrates and making their own power and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chongyin, commissioner of Heng-hai, wrote: "Hebei commissioners defied the court for sixty years because every county had garrison generals who seized power from prefects and magistrates and ruled as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 向使刺史各得行其職，則雖有奸雄如安、史，必不能以一州獨反也。

translations.literal: If prefects had each been able to perform their duties, then even with villains like An and Shi, they could not have rebelled alone with a single prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Had prefects been allowed to govern, even men as bold as An Lushan and Shi Siming could not have raised a single prefecture in revolt.

sentences.zh: 臣所領德、棣、景三州，已舉牒各還刺史職事，應在州兵並令刺史領之。」

translations.literal: In the three prefectures of De, Di, and Jing under my command, I have already submitted documents restoring each prefect to his duties, and all troops stationed in the prefectures are ordered to be led by the prefects."
translations.idiomatic: In De, Di, and Jing under my command I have already restored each prefect to his full duties and put all local troops under prefect command."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙寅，詔諸道節度、都團練、都防禦、經略等使所統支郡兵馬，並令刺史領之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingyin, an edict ordered that troops and horses in subordinate prefectures under military commissioners, grand regimental training commissioners, grand defense commissioners, frontier commissioners, and the like were all to be placed under prefect command.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on bingyin, an edict directed that all troops in subordinate prefectures under circuit commissioners, regimental training commissioners, defense commissioners, and frontier commissioners were to be led by the prefects.

sentences.zh: 自至德以來，節度使權重，所統諸州各置鎮兵，以大將主之，暴橫為患，故重胤論之。

translations.literal: Since the Zhide era, military commissioners had wielded great power; each prefecture under their command established garrison troops led by senior generals, whose violence and arrogance became a plague—hence Chongyin's memorial on the subject.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhide era military commissioners had grown overpowerful; every prefecture under them kept garrison troops commanded by senior generals who bullied the people—hence Chongyin's argument.

sentences.zh: 其後河北諸鎮，惟橫海最為順命，由重胤外之得宜故也。

translations.literal: Afterward among the Hebei garrison commands, only Heng-hai remained most obedient to the court—because beyond Chongyin's own conduct, matters were handled properly there.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, of all the Hebei garrisons, only Heng-hai stayed most loyal to the court—because Chongyin and his colleagues governed it well.

sentences.zh: 辛未，工部侍郎、同平章事程異薨。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Cheng Yi, vice minister of works and co–chief minister, died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Cheng Yi, vice minister of works and chief minister, died.

sentences.zh: 裴度在相位，知無不言，皇甫鎛之黨陰擠之。

translations.literal: While Pei Du served as chief minister, he spoke out whenever he knew something ought to be said; the faction of Huangfu Bo secretly undermined him.
translations.idiomatic: While Pei Du was chief minister he held nothing back when he knew the court should hear it; Huangfu Bo's faction worked quietly to force him out.

sentences.zh: 丙子，詔度以門下侍郎、同平章事，充河東節度使。

translations.literal: On bingzi, an edict appointed Du as vice director of the Secretariat and co–chief minister, and made him military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Pei Du was ordered to serve as vice director of the Secretariat and chief minister while taking command as military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 皇甫鎛專以掊克取媚，人無敢言者，獨諫議大夫武儒衡上疏言之。

translations.literal: Huangfu Bo relied solely on squeezing the people to win favor; no one dared speak against him—only Remonstrance Counselor Wu Ruheng submitted a memorial criticizing him.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo won favor by squeezing the people dry, and no one dared object—only Remonstrance Counselor Wu Ruheng memorialized the throne against him.

sentences.zh: 鎛自訴於上，上曰：「卿以儒衡上疏，將報怨邪！」

translations.literal: Bo complained to the emperor, who said, "Are you bringing this up because Ruheng submitted that memorial—you want revenge?"
translations.idiomatic: Bo complained to the emperor, who said, "Are you saying this because Ruheng memorialized against you—you want revenge?"

sentences.zh: 鎛乃不敢言。

translations.literal: Bo then dared say no more.
translations.idiomatic: Bo said no more.

sentences.zh: 儒衡，元衡之從父弟也。

translations.literal: Ruheng was a paternal cousin of Yuanheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ruheng was Wu Yuanheng's paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 史館修撰李翱上言，以為：「定禍亂者，武功也；

translations.literal: Academician Li Ao submitted a memorial, arguing: "It is martial achievement that settles calamity and disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Academician Li Ao submitted a memorial arguing that "martial force ends calamity and disorder;

sentences.zh: 興太平者，文德也。

translations.literal: it is civil virtue that brings forth great peace.
translations.idiomatic: civil virtue brings great peace.

sentences.zh: 今陛下既以武功定海內，若遂革弊事，復高祖、太宗舊制；

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already pacified the realm by martial force; if you would now reform abuses and restore the old institutions of Gaozu and Taizong;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has already pacified the realm by force of arms; if you would now root out abuses and restore the institutions of Gaozu and Taizong,

sentences.zh: 用忠正而不疑，屏邪佞而不邇；

translations.literal: employ the loyal and upright without doubt, and keep the wicked and flatterers at a distance;
translations.idiomatic: employ loyal men without suspicion and keep the wicked and flattering at arm's length;

sentences.zh: 改稅法，不督錢而納布帛；

translations.literal: revise the tax system so that cloth and silk are collected instead of pressing for cash;
translations.idiomatic: revise the tax laws to collect cloth and silk rather than pressing for cash;

sentences.zh: 絕進獻，寬百姓租賦；

translations.literal: end tribute offerings and lighten the people's rents and levies;
translations.idiomatic: end tribute presentations and lighten the people's rents and levies;

sentences.zh: 厚邊兵，以制戎狄侵盜；

translations.literal: strengthen frontier troops to check barbarian raids;
translations.idiomatic: strengthen frontier garrisons to check barbarian raids;

sentences.zh: 數訪問待制官，以通塞蔽；

translations.literal: frequently consult ad hoc policy advisers to open channels and remove blind spots;
translations.idiomatic: consult ad hoc policy advisers often to pierce obstruction and blind spots;

sentences.zh: 此六者，政之根本，太平所以興也。

translations.literal: these six measures are the root of government and the means by which great peace is achieved.
translations.idiomatic: these six are the roots of government and the foundation on which great peace is built.

sentences.zh: 陛下既已能行其難，若何不為其易乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already accomplished the difficult—why not do what is easy?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has already done what is hard—why not do what is easy?

sentences.zh: 以陛下天資上聖，如不惑近習容悅之辭，任骨鯁正直之士，與之興大化，可不勞而成也。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's heaven-given supreme wisdom, if you are not swayed by the words of nearby favorites who seek to please, and entrust hard-spoken upright men to work with you in launching great reform, it can be accomplished without great effort.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's heaven-sent wisdom, if you are not misled by the flattery of nearby favorites and instead entrust blunt, upright men to help launch great reform, it can be achieved without great strain.

sentences.zh: 若不有此為事，臣恐大功之後，逸欲易生。

translations.literal: If these things are not done, I fear that after this great achievement, indulgence and desire will easily arise.
translations.idiomatic: If these things are not done, I fear that after this great victory indulgence will come easily.

sentences.zh: 進言者必曰：『天下既平矣，陛下可以高枕自安逸。』

translations.literal: Those who speak to you will surely say: 'The realm is now at peace; Your Majesty may rest easy upon your pillow.'
translations.idiomatic: Those who advise you will say, 'The realm is at peace now; Your Majesty may rest easy.'

sentences.zh: 如是，則太平未可期矣！」

translations.literal: If so, great peace cannot be expected!"
translations.idiomatic: If that happens, great peace will never come!"

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁丑朔，田弘正送殺武元衡賊王士元等十六人，詔使內京兆府、御史台遍鞫之，皆款服。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day dingchou, Tian Hongzheng sent sixteen men including Wang Shiyuan, killers of Wu Yuanheng; an edict ordered the Capital Prefecture and the Censorate to conduct full interrogations within the capital, and all confessed.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, Tian Hongzheng sent up sixteen men including Wang Shiyuan, who had killed Wu Yuanheng; the court ordered the Capital Prefecture and the Censorate to interrogate them thoroughly in the capital, and all confessed.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹崔元略以元衡物色詢之，則多異同。

translations.literal: The capital prefect Cui Yuanlue questioned them according to Wu Yuanheng's descriptions, but accounts differed widely.
translations.idiomatic: Capital Prefect Cui Yuanlue questioned them using Wu Yuanheng's descriptions of the assailants, but their accounts diverged widely.

sentences.zh: 元略問其故，對曰：「恆、鄆同謀遣客刺元衡，而士元等後期，聞恆人事成，遂竊以為己功，還報受賞耳。

translations.literal: Yuanlue asked why; they replied, "Heng and Yan jointly plotted to send agents to assassinate Yuanheng, but Shiyuan and the others were late; hearing that the Heng affair had succeeded, they stole the credit for themselves and returned to report and receive rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlue asked why; they answered, "Heng and Yan plotted together to send assassins against Yuanheng, but Shiyuan and the others arrived late; hearing that the Heng side had succeeded, they stole the credit, went back, and collected the reward.

sentences.zh: 今自度為罪均，終不免死，故承之。」

translations.literal: Now judging that the guilt is equal and death cannot be avoided anyway, we admit it."
translations.idiomatic: Now we judge the guilt equal and know we cannot escape death anyway, so we confess."

sentences.zh: 上亦不欲復辨正，悉殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor also did not wish to reinvestigate further and had them all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not wish to investigate further and had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，宣武節度使韓弘始入朝，上待之甚厚。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Han Hong, military commissioner of Xuanwu, came to court for the first time; the emperor received him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Han Hong, military commissioner of Xuanwu, came to court for the first time and was received with great honor.

sentences.zh: 弘獻馬三千，絹五千，雜繒三萬，金銀器千，而汴之庫廄尚有錢百餘萬緡，絹百餘萬匹，馬七千匹，糧三百萬斛。

translations.literal: Hong presented three thousand horses, five thousand bolts of silk, thirty thousand assorted silks, and a thousand gold and silver vessels—yet Bian's treasuries and stables still held over a million strings of cash, over a million bolts of silk, seven thousand horses, and three million bushels of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Hong presented three thousand horses, five thousand bolts of silk, thirty thousand assorted silks, and a thousand gold and silver vessels—yet Bian's treasuries and stables still held more than a million strings of cash, more than a million bolts of silk, seven thousand horses, and three million bushels of grain.

sentences.zh: 己丑，群臣上尊號曰元和聖文神武法天應道皇帝，赦天下。

translations.literal: On jichou, the officials offered the honorific title "Emperor of the Yuanhe era, sage in civil and divine in martial virtue, conforming to Heaven and responding to the Way," and a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, the officials offered the honorific title "Emperor of the Yuanhe era, sage in civil and divine in martial virtue, conforming to Heaven and responding to the Way," and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 沂、海、兗、密觀察使王遂，本錢谷吏，性狷急，無遠識。

translations.literal: Wang Sui, commissioner of the Yi, Hai, Yan, and Mi circuit, had been a grain and revenue clerk by origin; he was narrow and quick-tempered, with no far-seeing judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui, commissioner of Yi, Hai, Yan, and Mi, had begun as a grain and revenue clerk; he was narrow and quick-tempered and lacked foresight.

sentences.zh: 時軍府草創，人情未安，遂專以嚴酷為治，所用杖絕大於常行者，每詈將卒，輒曰「反虜」；

translations.literal: At the time the army headquarters was newly established and morale unsettled; Sui governed solely through harsh severity—the clubs he used were far larger than usual, and whenever he cursed officers and men he called them "rebel bandits";
translations.idiomatic: The army headquarters was newly established and morale unsettled; Sui governed through harsh severity alone—the clubs he used were far larger than usual, and whenever he cursed officers and men he called them "rebel bandits";

sentences.zh: 又盛夏役士卒營府捨，督責峻急。

translations.literal: moreover, in the height of summer he put soldiers to work building headquarters buildings, driving them with fierce urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the height of summer he put soldiers to work building headquarters quarters and drove them with brutal urgency.

sentences.zh: 將卒憤怨。

translations.literal: Officers and men seethed with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，役卒王弁與其徒四人浴於沂水，密謀作亂，曰：「今服役觸罪亦死，奮命立事亦死，死於立事，不猶愈乎！

translations.literal: On xinmao, labor conscript Wang Bian and four followers bathed in the Yi River and secretly plotted revolt, saying, "Today, to serve on labor and commit an offense is still death; to risk your life and accomplish something is also death—is death in accomplishing something not better!
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, labor conscript Wang Bian and four companions bathed in the Yi River and secretly plotted rebellion, saying, "If we serve on labor and slip up we die; if we risk our lives and act we die too—isn't it better to die doing something?

sentences.zh: 明日，常侍與監軍、副使有宴，軍將皆在告，直兵多休息，吾屬乘此際出其不意取之，可以萬全。」

translations.literal: Tomorrow the commissioner will feast with the army supervisor and vice commissioner; the commanders will all be on leave and the guards mostly resting—we can take advantage of this moment and seize them by surprise; it can be done with full certainty."
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow the commissioner will feast with the army supervisor and vice commissioner; the commanders will all be on leave and most of the guards will be resting—we can strike by surprise and succeed with certainty."

sentences.zh: 四人皆以為然，約事成推弁為留後。

translations.literal: The four all agreed, and they agreed that if the plot succeeded, Bian would be made acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The four agreed, and they pledged that if the plot succeeded Bian would be made acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，遂方宴飲，日過中，弁等五人突入，於直房前取弓刀，逕前射副使張敦實，殺之。

translations.literal: On renchen, Sui was still feasting when the day had passed noon; Bian and the other five burst in, took bows and blades before the guard quarters, went straight forward and shot Vice Commissioner Zhang Dunshi, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, while Sui was still feasting past midday, Bian and four others burst in, seized bows and blades before the guard quarters, and shot Vice Commissioner Zhang Dunshi dead.

sentences.zh: 遂與監軍狼狽起走，弁執遂，數之以盛暑興役，用刑刻暴，立斬之。

translations.literal: Sui and the army supervisor fled in panic; Bian seized Sui, counted off his crimes of putting men to labor in fierce heat and his cruel severity in punishment, and had him beheaded on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Sui and the army supervisor fled in panic; Bian seized Sui, denounced him for putting men to labor in fierce heat and for cruel punishments, and had him beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 傳聲勿驚監軍，弁即自稱留後，升廳號令，與監軍抗禮，召集將吏參賀，眾莫敢不從。

translations.literal: Word was passed not to alarm the army supervisor; Bian at once styled himself acting commissioner, mounted the hall to issue orders, treated the army supervisor as an equal, and summoned officers and clerks to offer congratulations—none dared refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Word went out not to alarm the army supervisor; Bian at once styled himself acting commissioner, took the hall to issue orders, treated the army supervisor as an equal, and summoned officers and clerks to congratulate him—none dared refuse.

sentences.zh: 監軍具以狀聞。

translations.literal: The army supervisor reported the full situation to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor reported the whole affair to the court.

sentences.zh: 甲午，韓弘又獻絹二十五萬匹，絁三萬匹，銀器二百七十。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Han Hong again presented two hundred fifty thousand bolts of silk, thirty thousand bolts of coarse silk, and two hundred seventy silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Han Hong again presented two hundred fifty thousand bolts of silk, thirty thousand bolts of coarse silk, and two hundred seventy silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 左右軍中尉各獻錢萬緡。

translations.literal: The left and right palace army commissioners each presented ten thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right palace army commissioners each presented ten thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 自淮西用兵以來，度支、鹽鐵及四方爭進奉，謂之「助軍」；

translations.literal: Since the Huai-Xi campaign, the Finance Commission, Salt and Iron Bureau, and regions everywhere competed in presenting tribute, calling it "aid to the army";
translations.idiomatic: Since the Huai-Xi campaign, the Finance Commission, Salt and Iron Bureau, and regions everywhere competed in presenting tribute, calling it "aid to the army";

sentences.zh: 賊平又進奉，謂之「賀禮」；

translations.literal: when the rebels were pacified they presented again, calling it "congratulatory gifts";
translations.idiomatic: when the rebels were pacified they presented again, calling it "congratulatory gifts";

sentences.zh: 後又進奉，謂之「助賞」；

translations.literal: later they presented again, calling it "aid for rewards";
translations.idiomatic: later they presented again, calling it "aid for rewards";

sentences.zh: 上加尊號又進奉，亦，謂之「賀禮」。

translations.literal: when the emperor received his honorific title they presented again also, likewise calling it "congratulatory gifts."
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor received his honorific title they presented again, likewise calling it "congratulatory gifts."

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以河陽節度使令狐楚為中書侍郎，同平章事。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Linghu Chu, military commissioner of Heyang, was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and co–chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Linghu Chu, military commissioner of Heyang, was made vice director of the Secretariat and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 楚與皇甫鎛同年進士，引以為相。

translations.literal: Chu and Huangfu Bo had passed the jinshi examination in the same year; Bo brought him in as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and Huangfu Bo had passed the jinshi examination in the same year; Bo brought him in as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞沂州軍亂，甲辰，以棣州刺史曹華為沂、海、兗、密觀察使。

translations.literal: When the court heard of the military disturbance at Yizhou, on jiachen Cao Hua, prefect of Di, was appointed commissioner of the Yi, Hai, Yan, and Mi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard of the mutiny at Yizhou, on jiachen Cao Hua, prefect of Di, was appointed commissioner of Yi, Hai, Yan, and Mi.

sentences.zh: 韓弘累表請留京師。

translations.literal: Han Hong repeatedly submitted memorials asking to remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong repeatedly memorialized asking to remain in the capital.

sentences.zh: 八月，己酉，以弘守司徒，兼中書令。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiyou, Hong was made Situ in perpetuity and concurrently director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiyou, Hong was made Situ in perpetuity and concurrently director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以吏部尚書張弘靖同平章事，充宣武節度使。

translations.literal: On guichou, Zhang Hongjing, minister of civil personnel and co–chief minister, was made military commissioner of Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Zhang Hongjing, minister of civil personnel and chief minister, was made military commissioner of Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 弘靖，宰相子，少有令聞，立朝簡默。

translations.literal: Hongjing was a son of a chief minister; from youth he had a fine reputation, and in court he was brief and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing was the son of a chief minister; from youth he had a fine reputation, and in court he was brief and restrained.

sentences.zh: 河東、宣武闕帥，朝廷以其位望素重，使鎮之。

translations.literal: Hedong and Xuanwu both lacked commanders; the court, because their rank and prestige had long been weighty, sent them to take command.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong and Xuanwu both lacked commanders; the court sent men of long-standing rank and prestige to take command.

sentences.zh: 弘靖承王鍔聚斂之餘，韓弘嚴猛之後，兩鎮喜其廉謹寬大，故上下安之。

translations.literal: Hongjing took over after Wang E's hoarding and Han Hong's harsh rule; both garrisons welcomed his integrity, restraint, and generosity, and so all ranks were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing succeeded Wang E's hoarding and Han Hong's harsh rule; both garrisons welcomed his integrity, restraint, and generosity, and all ranks settled into peace.

sentences.zh: 己未，田弘正入朝，上待之尤厚。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Tian Hongzheng entered the capital; the emperor received him with especial favor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Tian Hongzheng came to court and was received with especial honor.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，陳許節度使郗士美薨，以庫部員外郎李渤為弔祭使。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Xi Shimei, military commissioner of Chen-Xu, died; Li Bo, vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, was made condolence envoy.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Xi Shimei, military commissioner of Chen-Xu, died; Li Bo, vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, was sent as condolence envoy.

sentences.zh: 渤上言：「臣過渭南，聞長源鄉舊四百戶，今才百餘戶，閺鄉縣舊三千戶，今才千戶，其它州縣大率相似。

translations.literal: Bo submitted a memorial: "When I passed Weinan, I heard that Changyuan township once had four hundred households and now has barely a hundred; Minxiang county once had three thousand households and now barely a thousand—the same pattern holds for other prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Bo submitted a memorial: "Passing Weinan, I heard that Changyuan township once had four hundred households and now has barely a hundred; Minxiang county once had three thousand and now barely a thousand—the same pattern holds across other prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 跡其所以然，皆由以逃戶稅攤於比鄰，致驅迫俱逃，此皆聚斂之臣剝下媚上，惟思竭澤，不慮無魚。

translations.literal: Tracing the causes, all stem from shifting absentee households' taxes onto neighbors, driving them to flee together—this is all the work of revenue-grinding ministers who strip the base to please those above, thinking only to drain the pond without considering there will be no fish left.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing the cause, it all stems from shifting fugitive households' taxes onto their neighbors, driving whole communities to flee together—work of revenue-grinding ministers who strip the people to please their superiors, draining the pond without thinking there will be no fish left.

sentences.zh: 乞降詔書，絕攤逃之弊。

translations.literal: I beg that an edict be issued to end the abuse of tax shifting for fugitive households.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that an edict be issued to end the abuse of shifting fugitive-household taxes onto neighbors.

sentences.zh: 盡逃戶之產償稅，不足者乞免之。

translations.literal: Let all fugitive households' property be used to pay taxes owed; where it is insufficient, I beg that exemptions be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Let fugitive households' property be used to pay what they owe, and where it is insufficient, grant exemptions.

sentences.zh: 計不數年，人皆復於農矣。」

translations.literal: Within a few years, by my reckoning, all would return to farming."
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years, by my reckoning, the people would return to farming."

sentences.zh: 執政見而惡之，渤遂謝病，歸東都。

translations.literal: When those in power saw it they despised it; Bo then resigned citing illness and returned to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When those in power saw it they took offense; Bo resigned citing illness and returned to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，吐蕃寇慶州，營於方渠。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Tibet raided Qingzhou and encamped at Fangqu.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Tibet raided Qingzhou and encamped at Fangqu.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議興兵討王弁，恐青、鄆相扇繼變，乃除弁開州刺史，遣中使賜以告身。

translations.literal: The court debated raising troops to punish Wang Bian, fearing Qing and Yan might incite each other into further revolts; they therefore appointed Bian prefect of Kaizhou and sent a palace envoy to present his commission.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated sending troops against Wang Bian but feared Qing and Yan might incite one another into further revolts; instead Bian was appointed prefect of Kaizhou and a palace envoy was sent with his commission.

sentences.zh: 中使紿之曰：「開州計已有人迎候道路，留後宜速發。」

translations.literal: The envoy deceived him, saying, "People should already be waiting along the road to Kaizhou; Acting Commissioner, you should set out at once."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy deceived him, saying, "People should already be waiting along the road to Kaizhou; Acting Commissioner, you should set out at once."

sentences.zh: 弁即日發沂州，導從尚百餘人，入徐州境，所在減之，其眾亦稍逃散，遂加以杻械，乘驢入關。

translations.literal: Bian departed Yizhou that same day with still over a hundred escorts; entering Xuzhou territory, they were reduced at each stop and his followers gradually scattered; he was then put in fetters and entered the pass riding a donkey.
translations.idiomatic: Bian left Yizhou that same day with more than a hundred escorts; once he entered Xuzhou territory his party was thinned at each stop and his followers gradually scattered; he was put in fetters and entered the pass riding a donkey.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊寅，腰斬東市。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuyin, he was cut in two at the waist in the eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuyin, he was cut in two at the waist in the eastern market.

sentences.zh: 先是，三分鄆兵以隸三鎮，及王遂死，朝廷以為師道餘黨凶態未除，命曹華引棣州兵赴鎮以討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yan troops had been divided in three and assigned to three garrisons; when Wang Sui died, the court believed Li Shidao's remnant followers' violent temperament had not been eliminated and ordered Cao Hua to lead Di prefecture troops to his post to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yan troops had been divided among three garrisons; when Wang Sui died, the court believed Li Shidao's remnant followers had not been subdued and ordered Cao Hua to bring Di prefecture troops to his post to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 沂州將士迎候者，華皆以好言撫之，使先入城，慰安其餘，眾皆不疑。

translations.literal: The officers and men of Yizhou who came to welcome him—Hua all soothed them with kind words, had them enter the city first, and reassured the rest; none suspected anything.
translations.idiomatic: The Yizhou officers and men who came to welcome him were all soothed with kind words; he had them enter the city first and reassured the rest, and none suspected anything.

sentences.zh: 華視事三日，大饗將士，伏甲士千人於幕下，乃集眾而諭之曰：「天子以鄆人有遷徙之勞，特加優給，宜令鄆人處右，沂人處左。」

translations.literal: On the third day of holding office, Hua held a great feast for the officers and men, concealed a thousand armored soldiers beneath the tent, then assembled the crowd and announced: "The Son of Heaven, because the Yan men have the hardship of relocation, has granted them special favor—they should take the places of honor on the right, and Yi men on the left."
translations.idiomatic: On his third day in office Hua held a great feast for the officers and men, concealed a thousand armored soldiers beneath the tent, then assembled the crowd and said, "The Son of Heaven, because the Yan men have the hardship of relocation, has granted them special favor—they should take the places of honor on the right and Yi men on the left."

sentences.zh: 既定，令沂人皆出，因闔門，謂鄆人曰：「王常侍以天子之命為帥於此，將士何得輒害之！」

translations.literal: When this was settled, he had all the Yi men leave, then closed the gates and said to the Yan men: "Commissioner Wang was appointed commander here by the Son of Heaven—how could officers and men rashly kill him!"
translations.idiomatic: When this was settled, he had all the Yi men leave, then closed the gates and said to the Yan men, "Commissioner Wang was appointed commander here by the Son of Heaven—how could officers and men rashly kill him!"

sentences.zh: 語未畢，伏者出，圍而殺之，死者千二百人，無一得脫者。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking, the hidden men emerged, surrounded them, and killed them—twelve hundred dead, not one escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished speaking, the hidden men emerged, surrounded them, and killed them—twelve hundred dead, not one escaped.

sentences.zh: 門屏間赤霧高丈餘，久之方散。

translations.literal: A red mist more than ten feet high rose between the gate and screen, and only after a long while did it disperse.
translations.idiomatic: A red mist more than ten feet high rose between the gate and screen and only after a long while dispersed.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：《春秋》書楚子虔誘蔡侯般殺之於申。

translations.literal: Commentator Sima Guang says: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that King Kang of Chu enticed Marquis Ban of Cai and killed him at Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Commentator Sima Guang says: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that King Kang of Chu enticed Marquis Ban of Cai and killed him at Shen.

sentences.zh: 彼列國也。

translations.literal: They were feudal states.
translations.idiomatic: They were feudal states.

sentences.zh: 孔子猶深貶之，惡其誘討也，況為天子而誘匹夫乎！

translations.literal: Confucius still condemned this deeply, hating such enticement in punitive action—how much more when one is Son of Heaven yet entices a common man!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius still condemned this deeply, hating enticement used in punishment—how much more when the Son of Heaven entices a common man!

sentences.zh: 王遂以聚斂之才，殿新造之邦，用苛虐致亂。

translations.literal: Wang Sui, with talents fit only for revenue-grubbing, was placed at the head of a newly formed command, and through harsh cruelty brought on disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui, with talents fit only for revenue-grubbing, was placed at the head of a newly formed command and brought on disorder through harsh cruelty.

sentences.zh: 王弁庸夫，乘釁竊發，苟沂帥得人，戮之易於犬豕耳，何必以天子詔書為誘人之餌乎！

translations.literal: Wang Bian was a common fellow who seized an opening to rebel—had Yizhou's commander been the right man, slaying him would have been easier than killing a dog or pig—why must an imperial edict be used as bait to lure a man!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bian was a common fellow who seized an opening to rebel—had Yizhou's commander been the right man, killing him would have been easier than slaughtering a dog or pig—why use an imperial edict as bait to lure a man!

sentences.zh: 且作亂者五人耳，乃使曹華設詐，屠千餘人，不亦濫乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, only five men rose in revolt—yet Cao Hua was allowed to set a trap and slaughter over a thousand—is that not excessive!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, only five men rose in revolt—yet Cao Hua was allowed to set a trap and slaughter more than a thousand—is that not excessive!

sentences.zh: 然則自今士卒孰不猜其將帥，將帥何以令其士卒！

translations.literal: From this time forth, which soldier will not suspect his commander—and how are commanders to command their soldiers!
translations.idiomatic: From this time forth, which soldier will not suspect his commander—and how are commanders to command their soldiers!

sentences.zh: 上下盻盻，如寇仇聚處，得間則更相魚肉，惟先發者為雄耳，禍亂何時而弭哉！

translations.literal: Above and below will eye each other warily, like enemies under one roof; given an opening they will prey on one another—and only whoever strikes first wins; when will calamity and disorder ever be stilled!
translations.idiomatic: Above and below will eye each other warily, like enemies under one roof; given an opening they will prey on one another—and only whoever strikes first wins; when will calamity and disorder ever be stilled!

sentences.zh: 惜夫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 憲宗削平僭亂，幾致治平，其美業所以不終，由苟徇近功，不敦大信故也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong suppressed rebellious pretenders and nearly achieved great order—yet his splendid enterprise did not reach completion because he was eager for quick success and did not uphold great trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong suppressed rebellious pretenders and nearly achieved great order—yet his splendid enterprise did not reach completion because he was eager for quick success and did not uphold great trustworthiness.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以田弘正兼侍中，魏博節度使如故。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Tian Hongzheng was also made palace attendant, while remaining military commissioner of Weibo as before.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Tian Hongzheng was also made palace attendant while remaining military commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 弘正三表請留，上不許。

translations.literal: Hongzheng three times submitted memorials asking to remain; the emperor did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng three times memorialized asking to remain; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 弘正常恐一旦物故，魏人猶以故事繼襲，故兄弟子侄皆仕諸朝，上皆擢居顯列，朱紫盈庭，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Hongzheng always feared that if he should die suddenly, Wei people would still inherit according to precedent; therefore his brothers, sons, and nephews all served in various courts, and the emperor promoted them all to prominent posts; vermillion and purple filled the hall, and people of the time took pride in it.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng lived in constant fear that if he died, the Wei clansmen would still press their hereditary claims. So he saw to it that his brothers, sons, and nephews all held office under successive regimes, and the emperor raised every one of them to high rank. Official robes in vermillion and purple filled the court, and contemporaries regarded the family with envy.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，上問宰相：「玄宗之政，先理而後亂，何也？」

translations.literal: On yisi, the emperor asked the chancellor: "Emperor Xuanzong's governance was orderly first and then chaotic — why?"
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, the emperor asked his chancellor, "Emperor Xuanzong's reign began in good order and ended in chaos. Why was that?"

sentences.zh: 崔群對曰：「玄宗用姚崇、宋璟、盧懷慎、蘇頲、韓休、張九齡則理，用宇文融、李林甫、楊國忠則亂。

translations.literal: Cui Qun replied: "When Xuanzong employed Yao Chong, Song Jing, Lu Huaishan, Su Ting, Han Xiu, and Zhang Jiuling, there was order; when he employed Yuwen Rong, Li Linfu, and Yang Guozhong, there was chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun answered, "When Xuanzong used men like Yao Chong, Song Jing, Lu Huaishan, Su Ting, Han Xiu, and Zhang Jiuling, the realm was well governed; when he turned to Yuwen Rong, Li Linfu, and Yang Guozhong, it fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 故用人得失，所繫非輕。

translations.literal: Thus the gain or loss in employing men — what is at stake is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: The choice of ministers, then, is no trifling matter.

sentences.zh: 人皆以天寶十四年安祿山反為亂之始，臣獨以為開元二十四年罷張九齡相，專任李林甫，此理亂之所分也。

translations.literal: People all take the An Lushan rebellion in the fourteenth year of Tianbao as the start of chaos; I alone hold that dismissing Zhang Jiuling as chancellor in the twenty-fourth year of Kaiyuan and giving sole charge to Li Linfu was where order and chaos divided.
translations.idiomatic: Most people date the collapse to An Lushan's rebellion in the fourteenth year of Tianbao, but I believe the turning point came in the twenty-fourth year of Kaiyuan, when Zhang Jiuling was removed from office and Li Linfu was given unchecked power. That was where good government gave way to ruin.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以開元初為法，以天寶末為戒，乃社稷無疆之福！」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will take the early Kaiyuan as model and the late Tianbao as warning — then the altars of state will enjoy limitless blessing!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty takes the early Kaiyuan years as your model and the late Tianbao years as your warning, the dynasty will know boundless good fortune."

sentences.zh: 皇甫鎛深恨之。

translations.literal: Huangfu Bo deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo took this as a deep personal affront.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬戊，容管奏安南賊楊清陷都護府，殺都護李象古及妻子、官屬、部曲千餘人。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renxu, Rongguan reported that the An Nan rebel Yang Qing seized the Protectorate headquarters, killing Protector-General Li Xianggu together with his wife, children, officials, and retinue — more than a thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on renxu, Rong Circuit reported that the An Nan rebel Yang Qing had overrun the protectorate headquarters and killed Protector-General Li Xianggu, his wife and children, his staff, and more than a thousand men of his command.

sentences.zh: 像古，道古之兄也，以貪縱苛刻失眾心。

translations.literal: Xianggu was Daogu's elder brother; through greed, indulgence, and harshness he lost the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggu was Daogu's elder brother. His greed, self-indulgence, and cruelty had long since cost him the loyalty of those under him.

sentences.zh: 清世為蠻酋，像古召為牙將，清鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: Qing had long been a tribal chieftain; Xianggu summoned him as a yajiang, and Qing was frustrated and unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Qing came from a long line of tribal chieftains. Xianggu brought him in as a staff officer, but Qing brooded over his thwarted ambitions.

sentences.zh: 像古命清將兵三千討黃洞蠻，清因人心怨怒，引兵夜還，襲府城，陷之。

translations.literal: Xianggu ordered Qing to lead three thousand troops against the Huangdong tribes; Qing, seizing on popular resentment, led his troops back by night, attacked the prefectural city, and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggu sent Qing at the head of three thousand men to campaign against the Huangdong tribes. Qing turned the men's resentment to his own purpose, marched back by night, stormed the prefectural seat, and took it.

sentences.zh: 初，蠻賊黃少卿，自貞元以來數反覆，桂管觀察使裴行立、容管經略使陽旻欲徼幸立功，爭請討之，上從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the tribal rebel Huang Shaoqing had repeatedly revolted since the Zhenyuan era; Guiguan Inspector Pei Xingli and Rongguan Commissioner Yang Min, seeking to win merit by luck, both vied to request a campaign against him, and the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble had begun with the tribal bandit Huang Shaoqing, who had risen and fallen repeatedly since the Zhenyuan era. Pei Xingli, inspector of Guiguan, and Yang Min, commissioner of Rongguan, each hoped to seize a quick victory and competed to ask for a punitive expedition. The emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 嶺南節度使孔戣屢諫曰：「此禽獸耳，但可自計利害，不足與論是非。」

translations.literal: Lingnan Military Commissioner Kong Kui repeatedly remonstrated, saying: "These are beasts — one can only calculate profit and loss for oneself; it is not worth debating right and wrong with them."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Kui, military commissioner of Lingnan, remonstrated again and again: "These people are no better than beasts. One weighs one's own costs and benefits — there is no point arguing morality with them."

sentences.zh: 上不聽，大發江、湖兵會容、桂二管入討，士卒被瘴癘，死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen; he massively mobilized troops from the Jiang and Hu regions to join the two circuits of Rong and Gui in the campaign; soldiers suffered from miasma, and the dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear of it. He raised a great army from the Yangzi and lake regions and sent it with the forces of Rong and Gui against the rebels. The troops were ravaged by miasma; the dead were beyond number.

sentences.zh: 安南乘之，遂殺都護。

translations.literal: An Nan took advantage of this and killed the Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: An Nan seized the moment and killed the protector-general.

sentences.zh: 行立、旻竟無功，二管凋弊，惟戣所部晏然。

translations.literal: Xingli and Min ultimately achieved nothing; the two circuits were devastated, while only Kong Kui's jurisdiction remained calm.
translations.idiomatic: Xingli and Min won nothing for all their effort. The two circuits were left in ruins, while only Kong Kui's territory remained undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以唐州刺史桂仲武為安南都護，赦楊清，以為瓊州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Gui Zhongwu, prefect of Tangzhou, was appointed Protector-General of An Nan; Yang Qing was pardoned and made prefect of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Gui Zhongwu, prefect of Tangzhou, was named protector-general of An Nan. Yang Qing was pardoned and appointed prefect of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 是月，吐蕃節度論三摩等將十五萬眾圍鹽州，党項亦發兵助之。

translations.literal: That month, the Tibetan commissioner Lun Sanmo and others led one hundred fifty thousand men to besiege Yanzhou; the Tangut also sent troops to assist.
translations.idiomatic: That same month, the Tibetan commander Lun Sanmo and his colleagues invested Yanzhou with a hundred and fifty thousand men, and the Tangut sent forces to support them.

sentences.zh: 刺史李文悅竭力拒守，凡二十七日，吐蕃不能克。

translations.literal: Prefect Li Wenyue exerted all his strength to resist; for twenty-seven days in all, the Tibetans could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Li Wenyue defended the city with everything he had. For twenty-seven days the Tibetans could not break in.

sentences.zh: 靈武牙將史奉敬言於朔方節度使杜叔良，請兵三千，繼三十日糧，深入吐蕃以解鹽州之圍。

translations.literal: Lingwu adjutant Shi Fengjing spoke to Shuofang Military Commissioner Du Shuliang, requesting three thousand troops with thirty days' rations to penetrate deep into Tibet and relieve the siege of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Fengjing, an adjutant at Lingwu, proposed to Du Shuliang, military commissioner of Shuofang, that he be given three thousand men and thirty days' supplies to strike deep into Tibetan territory and break the siege of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 叔良以二千五百人與之。

translations.literal: Shuliang gave him two thousand five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Shuliang gave him twenty-five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 奉敬行旬餘，無聲問，朔方人以為俱沒矣。

translations.literal: Fengjing marched for more than ten days with no word; the people of Shuofang thought all had perished.
translations.idiomatic: Fengjing marched for more than ten days without a word. In Shuofang everyone assumed the whole force was lost.

sentences.zh: 無何，奉敬自它道出吐蕃背，吐蕃大驚，潰去。

translations.literal: Before long, Fengjing emerged by another route behind the Tibetans; the Tibetans were greatly alarmed and broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Then, without warning, Fengjing appeared by another route in the Tibetans' rear. They panicked and broke camp.

sentences.zh: 奉敬奮擊，大破，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Fengjing struck vigorously and routed them; the casualties were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Fengjing pressed the attack and routed them utterly. The slain were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 奉敬與鳳翔將野詩良浦、涇原將郝玼以勇著名於邊，吐蕃憚之。

translations.literal: Fengjing, together with Fengxiang general Ye Shiliangpu and Jingyuan general Hao Qi, were famed on the frontier for courage; the Tibetans feared them.
