translations.idiomatic: Fengjing, Ye Shiliangpu of Fengxiang, and Hao Qi of Jingyuan were all celebrated on the frontier for their bravery, and the Tibetans feared them.

sentences.zh: 柳泌至台州，驅吏民採藥，歲餘，無所得而懼，舉家逃入山中。

translations.literal: Liu Bi arrived at Taizhou and drove officials and commoners to gather medicinal herbs; after more than a year with no results he grew afraid, and his whole family fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bi reached Taizhou he pressed officials and commoners into gathering herbs. After more than a year without success he grew frightened, and his whole household fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 浙東觀察使捕送京師。

translations.literal: The Zhedong inspector captured and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The inspector of Zhedong had him seized and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 皇甫鎛、李道古保護之，上復使待詔翰林；

translations.literal: Huangfu Bo and Li Daogu protected him, and the emperor again had him serve in the Hanlin awaiting edicts;
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo and Li Daogu shielded him, and the emperor restored him to the Hanlin as an attendant awaiting edicts;

sentences.zh: 服其藥，日加躁渴。

translations.literal: Taking his elixir, the emperor grew daily more irritable and thirsty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his elixirs and grew daily more irritable and feverishly thirsty.

sentences.zh: 起居舍人裴潾上言，以為：「除天下之害者受天下之利，同天下之樂者饗天下之福，自黃帝至於文、武，享國壽考，皆用此道也。

translations.literal: Attendant of Records Pei Lin submitted a memorial, arguing: "Those who remove the world's harm receive the world's benefit; those who share the world's joy enjoy the world's blessing — from the Yellow Emperor down to Wen and Wu, their long reigns and longevity all used this way.
translations.idiomatic: “Pei Lin, attendant of records, submitted a memorial arguing that those who remove the world's ills share in its blessings, and those who share the world's joys partake of its good fortune. From the Yellow Emperor down to Kings Wen and Wu, long reigns and long lives had all rested on that principle.

sentences.zh: 自去歲以來，所在多薦方士，轉相汲引，其數浸繁。

translations.literal: Since last year, everywhere many alchemists have been recommended, drawing on one another in succession; their number has gradually multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Since the previous year, alchemists had been recommended everywhere, each one bringing in others, and their numbers had steadily grown.

sentences.zh: 借令天下真有神仙，彼必深潛巖壑，惟畏人知。

translations.literal: Even if there truly were immortals in the world, they would surely hide deep in ravines and gorges, fearing only that people might know of them.
translations.idiomatic: Even if immortals truly existed, they would hide deep in the mountains and gorges and dread nothing so much as being found out.

sentences.zh: 凡候伺權貴之門，以大言自衒奇技驚眾者，皆不軌徇利之人，豈可信其說而餌其藥邪！

translations.literal: All who wait at the gates of the powerful, boasting with big talk and dazzling the crowd with strange arts — all are lawless men seeking profit; how can one trust their claims and take their elixirs!
translations.idiomatic: Men who haunt the doors of the powerful, trumpeting grand claims and dazzling crowds with strange tricks, are lawless profiteers. How can one believe their promises and swallow their drugs!

sentences.zh: 夫藥以愈疾，非朝夕常餌之物。

translations.literal: Medicine is for curing illness — it is not something to be taken daily as food.
translations.idiomatic: Medicine exists to cure sickness; it is not food to be taken morning and night.

sentences.zh: 況金石酷烈有毒，又益以火氣，殆非人五藏之所能勝也。

translations.literal: Moreover, metal and mineral compounds are fiercely toxic; compounded with fire treatment, they are scarcely what human organs can endure.
translations.idiomatic: Metal and mineral compounds are fiercely toxic to begin with, and when they are further refined by fire they are scarcely something the human body can bear.

sentences.zh: 古者君飲藥，臣先嘗之，乞令獻藥者先自餌一年，則真偽自可辨矣。」

translations.literal: In antiquity when a lord took medicine, a minister tasted it first; I beg that those who offer elixirs be made to take them themselves for a year first — then truth and falsehood would distinguish themselves."
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when a ruler took medicine, a minister tasted it first. I ask that anyone who offers an elixir be required to take it himself for a full year. Then truth and fraud would reveal themselves."

sentences.zh: 上怒，十一月，己亥，貶潾江陵令。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; in the eleventh month, on jihai, Pei Lin was demoted to magistrate of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. In the eleventh month, on jihai, Pei Lin was demoted to magistrate of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 初，群臣議上尊號，皇甫鎛欲增「孝德」字，中書侍郎、同平章事崔群曰：「言聖則孝在其中矣。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when ministers discussed an honorific title for the emperor, Huangfu Bo wished to add the characters "Xiao De"; Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Member of the Secretariat Cui Qun said: "To speak of sageness already includes filial piety within it."
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers were debating an honorific title for the emperor, Huangfu Bo wanted to add the words "Filial Virtue." Cui Qun, vice director of the Secretariat and co-member of the Secretariat, objected: "To call him sage already implies filial piety."

sentences.zh: 鎛譖群於上曰：「群於陛下惜『孝德』二字。」

translations.literal: Bo slandered Qun to the emperor, saying: "Qun begrudges Your Majesty the two characters 'Xiao De.'"
translations.idiomatic: Bo whispered to the emperor that Qun begrudged him the words "Filial Virtue."

sentences.zh: 上怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged.

sentences.zh: 時鎛給邊軍賜與，多不時得，又所給多陳敗，不可服用，軍士怒怒，流言欲為亂。

translations.literal: At the time Bo distributed border army rewards; they often did not receive them on time, and what was given was mostly old and rotten and unusable; the soldiers were furious, and rumors spread of planned rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Bo was distributing rewards to the frontier armies, but the men often received them late, and much of what arrived was rotten and useless. The soldiers were furious, and word spread that they meant to rebel.

sentences.zh: 李光顏憂懼，欲自殺。

translations.literal: Li Guangyan was worried and afraid and wished to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangyan was so distressed that he contemplated suicide.

sentences.zh: 遣人訴於上，上不信。

translations.literal: He sent someone to complain to the emperor; the emperor did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a messenger to plead with the emperor, but the emperor refused to believe him.

sentences.zh: 京師恟懼，群具以中外人情上聞。

translations.literal: The capital was alarmed; Qun fully reported the sentiments inside and outside to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Alarm spread through the capital, and Qun laid out the mood of court and country in full to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 鎛密言於上曰：「邊賜皆如舊制，而人情忽如此者，由群鼓扇，將以賣直，歸怨於上也。」

translations.literal: Bo secretly told the emperor: "Border rewards all follow the old system, yet sentiment suddenly turned like this because Qun is inciting it — he intends to sell his integrity and shift blame onto Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Bo secretly told the emperor, "The frontier rewards follow the old rules, yet sentiment has turned so suddenly only because Qun is stirring it up. He means to parade his integrity and lay the blame on Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this was so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙卯，以群為湖南觀察使，於是中外切齒於鎛矣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Qun was made Hunan inspector; from then on, inside and outside all gnashed teeth at Bo.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Qun was sent out as inspector of Hunan. From that day on, court and country alike seethed with hatred for Bo.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人武儒衡，有氣節，好直言，上器之，顧待甚渥，人皆言其且入相。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafter Wu Ruheng had integrity and spirit, loved to speak plainly; the emperor valued him and treated him most generously; everyone said he would soon enter the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ruheng, a drafter in the Secretariat, was a man of principle who spoke his mind. The emperor prized him and treated him with exceptional favor, and everyone said he would soon join the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 令狐楚忌之，思有以沮之者，乃薦山南東道節度推官狄兼謨才行。

translations.literal: Linghu Chu resented him and thought to obstruct him; he therefore recommended Di Jianmo, legal officer of the Shannan East Circuit, for his talent and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chu resented him and looked for a way to block his rise. He recommended Di Jianmo, a legal officer on the staff of the Shannan East Circuit, praising his talent and character.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，擢兼謨左拾遺內供奉。

translations.literal: On guihai, Jianmo was promoted to Left Reminder with inner palace appointment.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Jianmo was promoted to left reminder with an inner palace appointment.

sentences.zh: 兼謨，仁傑之族曾孫也。

translations.literal: Jianmo was a great-great-grandson of the Di clan of Renjie.
translations.idiomatic: Jianmo was a great-great-grandson of Di Renjie.

sentences.zh: 楚自草制辭，盛言「天後竊位，奸臣擅權，賴仁傑保佑中宗，克復明辟。」

translations.literal: Chu personally drafted the appointment decree, lavishly praising how "the Empress Dowager usurped the throne, wicked ministers seized power, and thanks to Renjie's protection of Zhongzong, the rightful sovereign was restored."
translations.idiomatic: Chu drafted the appointment edict himself, lavishing praise on how "the Empress Dowager usurped the throne and wicked ministers seized power, until Renjie protected Zhongzong and restored the rightful sovereign."

sentences.zh: 儒衡泣訴於上，且言：「臣曾祖平一，在天後朝，辭榮終老。」

translations.literal: Ruheng wept and complained to the emperor, further saying: "My great-grandfather Pingyi, in the Empress Dowager's reign, declined honor and lived out his days in retirement."
translations.idiomatic: Ruheng wept before the emperor and protested, adding, "My great-grandfather Pingyi, in the Empress Dowager's day, declined office and lived out his life in retirement."

sentences.zh: 上由是楚楚之為人。

translations.literal: The emperor from this came to despise Chu's character.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment the emperor looked on Chu with contempt.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年（

translations.literal: Fifteenth year of Yuanhe (
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Yuanhe (

sentences.zh: 庚子，公元八二零年）

translations.literal: gengzi, corresponding to 820 CE)
translations.idiomatic: the year gengzi, corresponding to 820 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，沂、海、兗、密觀察使曹華請徙理兗州，許之。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, Cao Hua, inspector of Yi, Hai, Yan, and Mi circuits, requested to move his seat to Yanzhou; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Cao Hua, inspector of the Yi, Hai, Yan, and Mi circuits, asked to move his headquarters to Yanzhou, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 義成節度使劉悟入朝。

translations.literal: Yicheng Military Commissioner Liu Wu came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu, military commissioner of Yicheng, came to court.

sentences.zh: 初，左軍中尉吐突承璀謀立澧王惲為太子，上不許。

translations.literal: Earlier, Left Army Director Tuhu Chengcui had plotted to install Prince Li of Li as crown prince; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Tuhu Chengcui, director of the Left Army, had plotted to make Prince Li of Li crown prince, but the emperor had refused.

sentences.zh: 及上寢疾，承璀謀尚未息。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell seriously ill, Chengcui's plotting had not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell gravely ill, Chengcui's scheming had not ceased.

sentences.zh: 太子聞而憂之，密遣人問計於司農卿郭釗。

translations.literal: The crown prince heard and was worried; he secretly sent someone to ask advice of Minister of Revenue Guo Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince heard of it and was alarmed. He secretly sent a messenger to ask Guo Zhao, minister of revenue, what he should do.

sentences.zh: 釗曰：「殿下但盡孝謹以俟之，勿恤其他。」

translations.literal: Zhao said: "Your Highness need only fulfill filial piety and caution and wait — do not worry about other matters."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "Your Highness has only to remain filial and careful and wait. Do not trouble yourself over anything else."

sentences.zh: 釗，太子之舅也。

translations.literal: Zhao was the crown prince's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was the crown prince's uncle on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 上服金丹，多躁怒，左右宦官往往獲罪，有死者，人人自危。

translations.literal: The emperor took gold elixir; he was often irritable and angry; eunuchs around him frequently incurred punishment, some dying; everyone felt endangered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was taking alchemical elixirs and grew ever more irritable and violent. The eunuchs around him were constantly punished, some even put to death, and everyone lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 庚子，暴崩於中和殿。

translations.literal: On gengzi, he suddenly died at the Zhonghe Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he died suddenly in the Zhonghe Hall.

sentences.zh: 時人皆言內常侍陳弘志弒逆，其黨類諱之，不敢討賊，但雲藥發，外人莫能明也。

translations.literal: People of the time all said Inner Attendant Chen Hongzhi committed regicide; his faction concealed it, dared not pursue the culprit, and only said the elixir had taken effect; outsiders could not know the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries widely believed that Inner Attendant Chen Hongzhi had murdered him. His accomplices covered it up, dared not pursue the killer, and said only that the elixir had taken effect. Outsiders had no way to know the truth.

sentences.zh: 中尉梁守謙與諸宦官馬進潭、劉承偕、韋元素、王守澄等共立太子，殺吐突承璀及澧王惲，賜左、右神策軍士錢人五十緡，六軍、威遠人三十緡，左、右金吾人十五緡。

translations.literal: Director Liang Shouqian together with eunuchs Ma Jintan, Liu Chengjie, Wei Yuansu, Wang Shoucheng, and others jointly installed the crown prince, killed Tuhu Chengcui and Prince Li of Li, and granted Left and Right Shence Army soldiers fifty strings of cash each, Six Armies and Weiyuan thirty each, and Left and Right Jinwu fifteen each.
translations.idiomatic: Director Liang Shouqian, together with the eunuchs Ma Jintan, Liu Chengjie, Wei Yuansu, Wang Shoucheng, and others, enthroned the crown prince, killed Tuhu Chengcui and Prince Li of Li, and distributed rewards: fifty strings of cash to each soldier of the Left and Right Shence Armies, thirty to the Six Armies and Weiyuan, and fifteen to the Left and Right Jinwu.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丙午，穆宗即位於太極殿東序。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, on bingwu, Muzong ascended the throne at the east wing of the Taiji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on bingwu, Muzong took the throne in the east wing of the Taiji Hall.

sentences.zh: 是日，召翰林學士段文昌等及兵部郎中薛放、駕部員外郎丁公著對于思政殿。

translations.literal: That day, he summoned Hanlin Academician Duan Wenchang and others, plus Bureau Director of Military Affairs Xue Fang and Deputy Director of the Riding Office Ding Gongzhu, for audience at the Sizheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he summoned the Hanlin academician Duan Wenchang and others, together with Xue Fang of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Ding Gongzhu of the Riding Office, for an audience in the Sizheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 放，戎之弟；

translations.literal: Fang was Rong's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Fang was Rong's younger brother;

sentences.zh: 公著，蘇州人；

translations.literal: Gongzhu was a native of Suzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu was a native of Suzhou;

sentences.zh: 皆太子侍讀也。

translations.literal: all had been tutors to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: both had served as tutors to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 上未聽政，放、公著常侍禁中，參預機密，上欲以為相，二人固辭。

translations.literal: The emperor had not yet taken up governance; Fang and Gongzhu regularly attended in the inner palace and participated in secret affairs; the emperor wished to make them chancellors, but both firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor had begun to hold court, Fang and Gongzhu attended him constantly in the inner palace and took part in confidential deliberations. The emperor wanted to make them chancellors, but both firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 丁未，輟西宮朝臨，集群臣於月華門外。

translations.literal: On dingwei, mourning audiences at the Western Palace were suspended; ministers were gathered outside the Yuehua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the mourning audiences at the Western Palace were suspended, and the ministers were assembled outside the Yuehua Gate.

sentences.zh: 貶皇甫鎛為崖州司戶，市井皆相賀。

translations.literal: Huangfu Bo was demoted to Revenue Clerk of Yazhou; commoners in the markets all congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo was demoted to revenue clerk of Yazhou, and people in the streets congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 上議命相，令狐楚薦御史中丞蕭俛。

translations.literal: The emperor discussed appointing chancellors; Linghu Chu recommended Censor-in-Chief Xiao Mian.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor discussed appointing chancellors, Linghu Chu recommended Xiao Mian, chief of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以俛及段文昌皆為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On xinhai, both Mian and Duan Wenchang were made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Co-Members of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, both Mian and Duan Wenchang were appointed vice directors of the Secretariat and co-members of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 楚、俛與皇甫鎛皆同年進士，上欲誅鎛，俛及宦官救之，故得免。

translations.literal: Chu, Mian, and Huangfu Bo had all passed the jinshi examination in the same year; the emperor wished to execute Bo; Mian and the eunuchs saved him, so he was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Chu, Mian, and Huangfu Bo had all passed the jinshi examination in the same year. The emperor wanted Bo executed, but Mian and the eunuchs intervened, and Bo was spared.

sentences.zh: 壬子，杖殺柳泌及僧大通，自餘方士皆流嶺表，貶左金吾將軍李道古循州司馬。

translations.literal: On renzi, Liu Bi and the monk Datong were beaten to death; all other alchemists were exiled to Lingnan; Left Jinwu General Li Daogu was demoted to Military Adjutant of Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Liu Bi and the monk Datong were beaten to death. All the other alchemists were exiled beyond the mountains, and Li Daogu, general of the Left Jinwu, was demoted to military adjutant of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以薛放為工部侍郎，丁公著為給事中。

translations.literal: On guichou, Xue Fang was made Vice Director of the Works Ministry, and Ding Gongzhu was made Chief Remonstrance Officer.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Xue Fang was appointed vice director of the Works Ministry and Ding Gongzhu was made chief remonstrance officer.

sentences.zh: 二月丁丑，乙卯，尊郭貴妃為皇太后上御丹鳳門樓，赦天下。

translations.literal: Second month, dingchou, yimao — Noble Consort Guo was honored as Empress Dowager; the emperor ascended the Danfeng Gate tower and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yimao, Noble Consort Guo was honored as empress dowager. The emperor ascended the Danfeng Gate tower and proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 事畢，盛陳倡優雜戲於門內而觀之。

translations.literal: When the ceremony was finished, entertainers and variety acts were lavishly arrayed inside the gate for viewing.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was over, he had singers, actors, and variety performers lavishly arrayed inside the gate and watched them perform.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，上幸左神策軍觀手搏雜戲。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the emperor visited the Left Shence Army to watch hand-to-hand combat and variety acts.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the emperor visited the Left Shence Army to watch wrestling and variety performances.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，監察御史楊虞卿上疏，以為：「陛下宜延對群臣，周遍顧問，惠以氣色，使進忠若趨利，論政若訴冤，如此而不致昇平者，未之有也。」

translations.literal: On gengyin, Investigating Censor Yang Yuqing submitted a memorial, arguing: "Your Majesty should extend audiences to ministers, inquire comprehensively, show a gracious countenance, so that offering loyalty is like pursuing profit and discussing governance is like airing grievances — if you do this and still fail to achieve peace, it has never happened."
translations.idiomatic: “On gengyin, Investigating Censor Yang Yuqing submitted a memorial arguing that the emperor ought to receive his ministers at length, question them thoroughly, and meet them with a gracious face, so that offering loyal counsel felt as natural as pursuing profit and discussing policy as urgent as pleading a grievance. If he did that and still failed to bring peace to the realm, it would be unprecedented.”

sentences.zh: 衡山人趙知微亦上疏諫上游畋無節。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhiwei of Hengshan also submitted a memorial remonstrating about the emperor's unrestrained hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhiwei of Hengshan also submitted a memorial remonstrating against the emperor's unrestrained hunting.

sentences.zh: 上雖不能用，亦不罪也。

translations.literal: Though the emperor could not adopt their advice, he did not punish them either.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not bring himself to follow their advice, but he did not punish them.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，廢邕管，命容管經略使陽旻兼領之。

translations.literal: On renchen, Yong Circuit was abolished; Rongguan Commissioner Yang Min was ordered to hold it concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Yong Circuit was abolished, and Yang Min, commissioner of Rongguan, was ordered to take charge of it as well.

sentences.zh: 安南都護桂仲武至安南，楊清拒境不納。

translations.literal: An Nan Protector-General Gui Zhongwu reached An Nan; Yang Qing barred the border and would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: When Protector-General Gui Zhongwu reached An Nan, Yang Qing closed the border and refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 清用刑慘虐，其黨離心。

translations.literal: Qing's use of punishment was cruel and brutal; his followers lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Qing ruled with cruel punishments, and his followers began to desert him.

sentences.zh: 仲武遣人說其酋豪，數月間，降者相繼，得兵七千餘人。

translations.literal: Zhongwu sent men to persuade tribal chieftains; within months, defectors came in succession, yielding over seven thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu sent envoys to win over the tribal chieftains. Within a few months defectors came in one after another, and he gathered more than seven thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以仲武為逗遛，甲午，以桂管觀察使裴行立為安南都護。

translations.literal: The court considered Zhongwu dilatory; on jiawu, Guiguan Inspector Pei Xingli was made An Nan Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged Zhongwu too slow to act. On jiawu, Pei Xingli, inspector of Guiguan, was appointed protector-general of An Nan.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以太僕卿杜式方為桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Minister of the Imperial Stud Du Shifang was made Guiguan inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Du Shifang, minister of the imperial stud, was made inspector of Guiguan.

sentences.zh: 丙申，貶仲武為安州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Zhongwu was demoted to prefect of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Zhongwu was demoted to prefect of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 丹王逾薨。

translations.literal: Prince Dan Yu died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dan Yu died.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃寇靈武。

translations.literal: Tibet raided Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans raided Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 憲宗之末，回鶻遣合達干來求婚尤切，憲宗許之。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xianzong's reign, the Uyghurs sent Hegedagan to request marriage with especial urgency; Xianzong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Xianzong's reign, the Uyghurs sent Hegedagan to press a marriage alliance with unusual urgency, and Xianzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸卯朔，遣合達干歸國。

translations.literal: Third month, on the first day guimao, Hegedagan was sent home.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day of the cycle, guimao, Hegedagan was sent back to his country.

sentences.zh: 上見夏州觀察判官柳公權書跡，愛之。

translations.literal: The emperor saw the calligraphy of Xiazhou observation aide Liu Gongquan and admired it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the calligraphy of Liu Gongquan, an aide on the staff of the Xiazhou inspector, and admired it.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以公權為右拾遺、翰林侍書學士。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Gongquan was made Right Reminder and Hanlin Calligraphy Academician.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Gongquan was appointed right reminder and Hanlin calligraphy academician.

sentences.zh: 上問公權：「卿書何能如是之善？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Gongquan: "How can your writing be so excellent?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Gongquan, "How is it that your writing can be so fine?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「用筆在心，心正則筆正。」

translations.literal: He replied: "The brush is used with the heart; when the heart is upright, the brush is upright."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The brush follows the heart; when the heart is true, the brush is true."

sentences.zh: 上默然改容，知其以筆諫也。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent and changed expression, understanding that he was remonstrating through calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent, his face changing; he understood that Gongquan was remonstrating through his brush.

sentences.zh: 公權，公綽之弟也。

translations.literal: Gongquan was Gongchuo's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan was the younger brother of Gongchuo.

sentences.zh: 辛未，安南將士開城納桂仲武，執楊清，斬之。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Annan soldiers and officers opened the city and admitted Gui Zhongwu, seized Yang Qing, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Annan troops opened the city gates to Gui Zhongwu, seized Yang Qing, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 裴行立至海門而卒。

translations.literal: Pei Xingli reached Haimen and died.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingli reached Haimen and died there.

sentences.zh: 復以仲武為安南都護。

translations.literal: Zhongwu was again made protector-general of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu was again appointed protector-general of Annan.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃寇鹽州。

translations.literal: Tibetans raided Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans raided Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，膳部員外郎元稹為江陵士曹，與監軍崔潭峻善。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuan Zhen, vice director of the Bureau of Provisioners, had served as legal aide at Jiangling and was on good terms with the army supervisor Cui Tanjun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuan Zhen, vice director of the Bureau of Provisioners, had served as a legal aide at Jiangling and was close to the army supervisor Cui Tanjun.

sentences.zh: 上在東宮，聞宮人誦稹歌詩而善之。

translations.literal: When the emperor was crown prince, he heard palace women reciting Zhen's songs and poems and admired them.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was still crown prince, he heard palace women reciting Zhen's songs and poems and admired them.

sentences.zh: 及即位，潭峻歸朝，獻稹歌詩百餘篇。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Tanjun returned to court and presented more than a hundred of Zhen's songs and poems.
translations.idiomatic: After his accession, Tanjun returned to court and presented more than a hundred of Zhen's songs and poems.

sentences.zh: 上問：「稹安在？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "Where is Zhen?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Where is Zhen?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「今為散郎。」

translations.literal: The reply was: "He is now a supernumerary official."
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: "He is now a supernumerary official."

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，庚戌，以稹為祠部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on gengxu, Zhen was made bureau director of the Ministry of Rites and put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on gengxu, Zhen was appointed bureau director of the Ministry of Rites and put in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 朝論鄙之。

translations.literal: Court opinion despised this.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 會同傣食瓜於閣下，有蠅集其上，中書舍人武儒衡以扇揮之曰：「適從何來，遽集於此！」

translations.literal: Once when colleagues were eating melon under the pavilion and flies gathered on it, Vice Minister Wu Ruheng waved a fan at them and said: "Where have you just come from, to gather here so suddenly!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, as colleagues were eating melon under the pavilion and flies gathered on it, Vice Minister Wu Ruheng fanned them away and said, "Where did you just come from, to swarm here so suddenly!"

sentences.zh: 同僚皆失色，儒衡意氣自若。

translations.literal: The colleagues all changed color; Ruheng remained perfectly composed.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues all blanched, but Ruheng remained perfectly at ease.

sentences.zh: 庚申，葬神聖章武孝皇帝於景陵，廟號憲宗。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the Divine Sacred Filial Martial Emperor was buried at Jing Mausoleum; his temple name was Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the Divine Sacred Filial Martial Emperor was buried at Jing Mausoleum; his temple name was Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 六月，以湖南觀察使崔群為吏部侍郎，召對別殿。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Cui Qun, governor of Hunan, was made vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and summoned for audience in a separate hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Cui Qun, governor of Hunan, was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and summoned to audience in a separate hall.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕升儲副，知卿為羽翼。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When I was elevated as heir apparent, I knew you were my support."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When I was made heir apparent, I knew you were my ally."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「先帝之意，久屬聖明，臣何力之有！」

translations.literal: He replied: "The late emperor's intent had long rested on Your Sagacious Majesty—what strength did I have!"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The late emperor's choice had long rested on Your Sagacious Majesty—what credit can I claim!"

sentences.zh: 太后居興慶宮，每朔望，上帥百官詣宮上壽。

translations.literal: The empress dowager resided at Xingqing Palace; on each new and full moon, the emperor led the hundred officials to the palace to offer felicitations.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager lived at Xingqing Palace; on each new and full moon, the emperor led the officials to the palace to offer birthday felicitations.

sentences.zh: 上性侈，所以奉養太后尤為華靡。

translations.literal: The emperor was extravagant by nature, and his provision for the empress dowager was especially lavish.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was extravagant by nature, and his care for the empress dowager was especially sumptuous.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙巳，以鄆、曹、濮節度為天平軍。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on yisi, the Yuncao-Pu military command was reorganized as the Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on yisi, the Yuncao-Pu command was reorganized as the Tianping Army.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎、同平章事令狐楚坐為山陵使，部吏盜官物，又不給工人傭直，收其錢十五萬緡為羨餘獻之，怨訴盈路。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Chief Minister Linghu Chu was punished because, as overseer of the imperial mausoleum, his subordinates stole government goods and he failed to pay workers' wages, instead collecting one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash as surplus to present to the throne; complaints of injustice filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Chief Minister Linghu Chu was punished because, as overseer of the imperial mausoleum, his staff stole government goods and he failed to pay workers' wages, instead pocketing one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash as surplus to present to the throne; complaints of injustice filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，罷為宣、歙、池觀察使。

translations.literal: On dingmao, he was removed and made governor of Xuan, She, and Chi.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, he was dismissed and made governor of Xuan, She, and Chi.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸已，發神策兵二千浚魚藻池。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on guisi, two thousand Shence troops were dispatched to dredge the Yuzao Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guisi, two thousand Shence troops were sent to dredge the Yuzao Pool.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以御史中丞崔植為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Censor-in-Chief Cui Zhi was made Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Censor-in-Chief Cui Zhi was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 己亥，再貶令狐楚衡州刺史。

translations.literal: On jihai, Linghu Chu was again demoted to prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Linghu Chu was demoted again to prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 上甫過公除，即事游畋聲色，賜與無節。

translations.literal: The emperor had scarcely passed the period of official mourning when he turned to hunting, pleasure, and music, bestowing gifts without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had barely completed the mourning period when he took up hunting, music, and pleasure, lavishing gifts without restraint.

sentences.zh: 九月，欲以重陽大宴。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he wished to hold a grand banquet for the Double Ninth Festival.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, he planned a grand banquet for the Double Ninth Festival.

sentences.zh: 拾遺李玨帥其同僚上疏曰：「伏以元朔未改，園陵尚新，雖陛下就易月之期，俯從人欲；

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Li Jue led his colleagues in submitting a memorial: "We consider that the new year has not yet changed and the imperial tombs are still fresh; though Your Majesty accedes to the month of reduced mourning and bends to popular desire;
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Li Jue led his colleagues in submitting a memorial: "We note that the new year has not yet begun and the imperial tombs are still fresh; though Your Majesty has entered the month of reduced mourning and yielded to popular desire,

sentences.zh: 而《禮經》著三年之制，猶服心喪。

translations.literal: yet the Book of Rites prescribes the three-year rule, and one still wears mourning in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: the Book of Rites still prescribes three years of mourning, and the heart remains in mourning.

sentences.zh: 遵同軌之會始離京，告遠夷之使未覆命。

translations.literal: The gathering at Tonggui has only just left the capital, and envoys announcing to distant barbarians have not yet returned with replies.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly at Tonggui has only just departed the capital, and envoys sent to announce the death to distant peoples have not yet returned.

sentences.zh: 遏密弛禁，蓋為齊人。

translations.literal: Loosening the solemn restraints was done for the sake of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Relaxing the mourning restrictions was meant for the common people.

sentences.zh: 合謀後庭，事將未可。」

translations.literal: To conspire for a banquet in the inner quarters—the matter truly cannot be approved."
translations.idiomatic: To plan a grand feast in the inner palace—this truly cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 上不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 戊午，加邠寧節度使李光顏、武寧節度使李愬並同平章事。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Li Guangyan, military commissioner of Binning, and Li Su, military commissioner of Wuning, were both given the title of Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Li Guangyan, military commissioner of Binning, and Li Su, military commissioner of Wuning, were both made chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，王承宗薨，其下秘不發喪，子知感、知信皆在朝，諸將欲取帥於屬內諸州。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Wang Chengzong died; his subordinates kept the death secret and did not announce mourning; his sons Zhigan and Zhixin were both at court; the generals wished to choose a commander from among the prefectures under their jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Wang Chengzong died; his subordinates concealed the death and did not announce mourning; his sons Zhigan and Zhixin were both at court; the generals wanted to choose a new commander from among the prefectures under their control.

sentences.zh: 參謀崔燧以承宗祖母涼國夫人命，告諭諸將及親兵，立承宗之弟觀察支使承元。

translations.literal: Staff officer Cui Sui, by order of Chengzong's grandmother the Lady of Liang State, announced to the generals and personal troops and installed Chengzong's younger brother Chengyuan, administrative aide to the governor.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Cui Sui, acting on orders from Chengzong's grandmother, the Lady of Liang State, announced to the generals and personal troops and installed Chengzong's younger brother Chengyuan, an administrative aide in the governor's office.

sentences.zh: 承元時年二十，將士拜之，承元不受，泣且拜，諸將固請不已。

translations.literal: Chengyuan was then twenty years old; the officers bowed to him, but Chengyuan refused, weeping and bowing in return; the generals pressed him without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyuan was then twenty; the officers bowed to him, but he refused, weeping and bowing in return; the generals pressed him again and again.

sentences.zh: 承元曰：「天子遣中使監軍，有事當與之議。」

translations.literal: Chengyuan said: "The Son of Heaven has sent a palace envoy to supervise the army; when there is business it should be discussed with him."
translations.idiomatic: Chengyuan said, "The Son of Heaven has sent a palace envoy to supervise the army; when there is business, it should be discussed with him."

sentences.zh: 及監軍至，亦勸之。

translations.literal: When the army supervisor arrived, he too urged him to accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the army supervisor arrived, he too urged him to accept.

sentences.zh: 承元曰：「諸公未忘先德，不以承元年少，欲使之攝軍務，承元請盡節天子以遵忠烈王之志，諸公肯從之乎！」

translations.literal: Chengyuan said: "You gentlemen have not forgotten our forebear's virtue; though Chengyuan is young, you wish him to administer military affairs—I ask to devote myself fully to the Son of Heaven and follow the will of the Loyal and Valiant Prince—will you gentlemen consent?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengyuan said, "You gentlemen have not forgotten our forebear's virtue; though I am young, you wish me to administer military affairs—I ask to devote myself fully to the Son of Heaven and follow the will of the Loyal and Valiant Prince—will you consent?"

sentences.zh: 眾許諾。

translations.literal: The assembly assented.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly assented.

sentences.zh: 承元乃視事於都將聽事，令左右不得謂己為留後，委事於參佐，密表請朝廷除帥。

translations.literal: Chengyuan then conducted affairs in the chief general's hall, ordered those around him not to call him acting commander, entrusted business to his staff, and secretly memorialized requesting that the court appoint a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyuan then took up duties in the chief general's hall, forbade those around him to call him acting commander, delegated affairs to his staff, and secretly memorialized asking the court to appoint a commander.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，監軍奏承宗疾亟，弟承元權知留後，並以承元表聞。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the army supervisor reported that Chengzong was gravely ill and his brother Chengyuan was temporarily managing as acting commander, and also forwarded Chengyuan's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, the army supervisor reported that Chengzong was gravely ill and his brother Chengyuan was temporarily acting as commander, and forwarded Chengyuan's memorial.

sentences.zh: 党項復引吐蕃寇涇州，連營五十里。

translations.literal: The Tangut again led Tibetans to raid Jingzhou, their camps stretching for fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut again led Tibetans to raid Jingzhou, their camps stretching for fifty li.

sentences.zh: 辛已，遣起居舍人拍耆詣鎮州宣慰。

translations.literal: On xinsi, attendant recorder Bai Qi was dispatched to Zhenzhou to proclaim consolation.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, attendant recorder Bai Qi was dispatched to Zhenzhou to proclaim consolation.

sentences.zh: 壬午，群臣入閣。

translations.literal: On renwu, the ministers entered the privy council hall.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, the ministers entered the privy council hall.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫鄭覃、崔郾等五人進言：「陛下宴樂過多，畋游無度。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials Zheng Tan, Cui Yan, and five others advanced to speak: "Your Majesty's feasting and music are excessive, and hunting knows no bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials Zheng Tan, Cui Yan, and five others stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty's feasting and music are excessive, and your hunting knows no bounds.

sentences.zh: 今胡寇壓境，忽有急奏，不知乘輿所在。

translations.literal: Now barbarian raiders press the borders; if an urgent memorial suddenly arrives, no one will know where the imperial carriage is.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian raiders now press the borders; if an urgent report suddenly arrives, no one will know where the imperial carriage is.

sentences.zh: 又晨夕與近習倡優狎暱，賜與過厚。

translations.literal: Moreover, morning and evening you are intimate with favorites, entertainers, and performers, bestowing rewards far too generously.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, morning and evening you are intimate with favorites, entertainers, and performers, bestowing rewards far too lavishly.

sentences.zh: 大金帛皆百姓膏血，非有功不可與。

translations.literal: Great gold and silk are all the flesh and blood of the common people—without merit they should not be given.
translations.idiomatic: Great stores of gold and silk are the flesh and blood of the people—they should not be given without merit.

sentences.zh: 雖內藏有餘，願陛下愛之，萬一四方有事，不復使有司重斂百姓。」

translations.literal: Though the inner treasury may have surplus, we beg Your Majesty to cherish it, so that if someday there is trouble in the four directions, officials need not again heavily levy the people."
translations.idiomatic: Though the inner treasury may have surplus, we beg Your Majesty to guard it carefully, so that if trouble arises in the four directions, officials need not again heavily levy the people."

sentences.zh: 時久無閣中論事者，上始甚訝之，謂宰相曰：「此輩何人？」

translations.literal: It had been long since anyone spoke on business in the privy council; the emperor was at first greatly surprised and said to the chief ministers: "Who are these people?"
translations.idiomatic: It had been long since anyone spoke on business in the privy council; the emperor was at first greatly surprised and said to the chief ministers, "Who are these people?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「諫官。」

translations.literal: The reply was: "Remonstrance officials."
translations.idiomatic: The answer was, "Remonstrance officials."

sentences.zh: 上乃使人慰勞之，曰：「當依卿言。」

translations.literal: The emperor then sent someone to comfort them, saying: "I shall follow your words."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent someone to comfort them, saying, "I shall follow your advice."

sentences.zh: 宰相皆賀，然實不能用也。

translations.literal: The chief ministers all congratulated one another, but in fact he could not put the advice into practice.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers all congratulated one another, but in fact the emperor could not act on the advice.

sentences.zh: 覃，珣瑜之子也。

translations.literal: Tan was Xunyu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was the son of Xunyu.

sentences.zh: 上嘗謂給事中丁公著曰：「聞外間人多宴樂，此乃時和人安，足用為慰。」

translations.literal: The emperor once said to Attendant-in-Ordinary Ding Gongzhu: "I hear that many people outside are feasting and making merry—this shows the times are harmonious and the people at peace, enough to be reassuring."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said to Attendant-in-Ordinary Ding Gongzhu, "I hear that many people outside are feasting and making merry—this shows the times are harmonious and the people at peace, enough to be reassuring."

sentences.zh: 公著對曰：「此非佳事，恐漸勞聖慮。」

translations.literal: Gongzhu replied: "This is not a good thing; I fear it will gradually burden Your Majesty with cares."
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu replied, "This is not a good thing; I fear it will gradually burden Your Majesty with cares."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何故？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Why?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「自天寶以來，公卿大夫競為游宴，沉酣晝夜，優雜子女，不愧左右。

translations.literal: He replied: "Since the Tianbao era, high and low officials have vied in pleasure outings, drowning in revelry day and night, mixing with singers and dancers, unashamed before those at their side.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Since the Tianbao era, officials high and low have vied in pleasure outings, drowning in revelry day and night, mixing with singers and dancers, unashamed before those at their side.

sentences.zh: 如此不已，則百職皆廢，陛下能無獨憂勞乎！

translations.literal: If this continues without end, every office will fall into neglect—can Your Majesty avoid bearing all the worry and toil alone!
translations.idiomatic: If this continues without end, every office will fall into neglect—can Your Majesty avoid bearing all the worry and toil alone!

sentences.zh: 願少加禁止，乃天下之福也。」

translations.literal: I beg that it be somewhat restrained—that would be fortune for all under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that it be somewhat restrained—that would be fortune for all under heaven."

sentences.zh: 癸未，涇州奏吐蕃進營距州三十里，告急求救。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Jingzhou reported that Tibetans had advanced their camps to within thirty li of the prefecture and urgently sought rescue.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Jingzhou reported that Tibetans had advanced their camps to within thirty li of the city and urgently sought rescue.

sentences.zh: 以右軍中尉梁守謙為左、右神策京西、北行營都監，將兵四千人，並發八鎮全軍救之。

translations.literal: Right Inner Palace Commander Liang Shouqian was made overall supervisor of the Left and Right Shence western and northern expeditionary camps, leading four thousand troops, and the full armies of the eight garrisons were also mobilized to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Right Inner Palace Commander Liang Shouqian was made overall supervisor of the Left and Right Shence western and northern expeditionary camps, leading four thousand troops, and the full armies of the eight garrisons were also mobilized to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 賜將士裝錢二萬緡。

translations.literal: The soldiers were given twenty thousand strings of cash for equipment.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were given twenty thousand strings of cash for equipment.

sentences.zh: 以郯王府長史邵同為太府少卿兼御史中丞，充答吐蕃請和好使。

translations.literal: Shao Tong, chief administrator of the Prince of Tan's household, was made vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and concurrently censor-in-chief, serving as envoy to respond to Tibet's request for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Tong, chief administrator of the Prince of Tan's household, was appointed vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and concurrently censor-in-chief, serving as envoy to respond to Tibet's request for peace.

sentences.zh: 初，秘書少監田洎入吐蕃為弔祭使，吐蕃請與唐盟於長武城下，洎恐吐蕃留之不得還，唯阿而已。

translations.literal: Earlier, Vice Director of the Secretariat Tian Ji entered Tibet as mourning envoy; Tibet requested to ally with Tang below Changwu city; Ji feared Tibet would detain him and never return, and merely agreed evasively.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Vice Director of the Secretariat Tian Ji had entered Tibet as a mourning envoy; Tibet requested to ally with Tang below Changwu city; Ji feared Tibet would detain him and merely agreed evasively.

sentences.zh: 既而吐蕃為党項所引入寇，因以為辭曰：「田洎許我將兵赴盟。」

translations.literal: Before long Tibet, led by the Tangut, invaded; they used this as a pretext, saying: "Tian Ji promised we could bring troops to the alliance."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tibet, led by the Tangut, invaded; they used this as a pretext, saying, "Tian Ji promised we could bring troops to the alliance."

sentences.zh: 於是貶洎郴州司戶。

translations.literal: Ji was therefore demoted to registrar of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was therefore demoted to registrar of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 成德軍始奏王承宗薨。

translations.literal: The Chengde army first reported that Wang Chengzong had died.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengde army first reported that Wang Chengzong had died.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，徙田弘正為成德節度使，以王承元為義成節度使，劉悟為昭義節度使，李愬為魏博節度使。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Tian Hongzheng was transferred to military commissioner of Chengde; Wang Chengyuan was made military commissioner of Yicheng; Liu Wu was made military commissioner of Zhaoyi; Li Su was made military commissioner of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Tian Hongzheng was transferred to military commissioner of Chengde; Wang Chengyuan was made military commissioner of Yicheng; Liu Wu was made military commissioner of Zhaoyi; and Li Su was made military commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 又以左金吾將軍田布為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: Left Jinwu General Tian Bu was also made military commissioner of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Left Jinwu General Tian Bu was also appointed military commissioner of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 渭州刺史郝玼出兵襲吐蕃營，所殺甚眾。

translations.literal: Hao Bi, prefect of Weizhou, sent troops to strike the Tibetan camp and killed a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Bi, prefect of Weizhou, sent troops to strike the Tibetan camp and killed a great many.

sentences.zh: 李光顏發邠寧兵救涇州。

translations.literal: Li Guangyan mobilized Binning troops to rescue Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangyan mobilized Binning troops to rescue Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 邠寧兵以神策受賞厚，皆慍曰：「人給五十緡而不識戰鬥者，彼何人邪！

translations.literal: Binning soldiers, resentful that the Shence Army received rich rewards, all said angrily: "Those who get fifty strings apiece and don't know how to fight—who are they!
translations.idiomatic: Binning soldiers, resentful that the Shence Army received rich rewards, all said angrily, "Those who get fifty strings apiece and don't know how to fight—who are they!

sentences.zh: 常額衣資不得而前冒白刃者，此何人邪！」

translations.literal: Those who can't even get their regular clothing allowance yet rush ahead under naked blades—who are we!"
translations.idiomatic: Those who can't even get their regular clothing allowance yet rush ahead under naked blades—who are we!"

sentences.zh: 洶洶不可止。

translations.literal: The uproar could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The uproar could not be stopped.

sentences.zh: 光顏親為開陳大義以諭之，言與涕俱，然後軍士感悅而行。

translations.literal: Guangyan personally expounded the greater principle to them, speaking through tears; only then were the soldiers moved and pleased to march.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan personally expounded the greater principle to them, speaking through tears; only then were the soldiers moved and willing to march.

sentences.zh: 將至涇州，吐蕃懼而退。

translations.literal: When they were nearing Jingzhou, the Tibetans feared them and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When they were nearing Jingzhou, the Tibetans feared them and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，罷神策行營。

translations.literal: On bingxu, the Shence expeditionary camp was disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, the Shence expeditionary camp was disbanded.

sentences.zh: 西川奏吐蕃寇雅州。

translations.literal: Sichuan reported that Tibetans raided Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan reported that the Tibetans raided Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，鹽州奏吐蕃營於烏、白池，尋亦皆退。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Yanzhou reported that Tibetans had camped at the Black and White Pools, but soon all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Yanzhou reported that Tibetans had camped at the Black and White Pools, but soon all withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸卯，遣諫議大夫鄭覃詣鎮州宣慰，賜錢一百萬緡以賞將士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on guimao, Remonstrance Official Zheng Tan was dispatched to Zhenzhou to proclaim consolation, and one million strings of cash were bestowed to reward the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on guimao, Remonstrance Official Zheng Tan was dispatched to Zhenzhou to proclaim consolation, and one million strings of cash were bestowed to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 王承元既請朝命，諸將及鄰道爭以故事勸之，承元皆不聽。

translations.literal: After Wang Chengyuan had requested an imperial appointment, generals and neighboring circuits all urged him by precedent to resist, but Chengyuan refused to listen to any of them.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Chengyuan had requested an imperial appointment, generals and neighboring circuits all urged him by precedent to resist, but Chengyuan would listen to none of them.

sentences.zh: 及移鎮義成，將士喧嘩不受命，承元與柏耆召諸將以詔旨諭之，諸將號哭不從。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to command Yicheng, the officers clamored and refused to accept the order; Chengyuan and Bai Qi summoned the generals and explained the imperial decree, but the generals wailed and would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to Yicheng, the officers clamored and refused to accept the order; Chengyuan and Bai Qi summoned the generals and explained the imperial decree, but the generals wailed and would not obey.

sentences.zh: 承元出家財以散之，擇其有勞者擢之，謂曰：「諸公以先代之故，不欲承元去，此意甚厚。

translations.literal: Chengyuan distributed his family wealth among them, selected those who had merit and promoted them, and said: "You gentlemen, out of regard for our forebears, do not wish Chengyuan to leave—this feeling is very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyuan distributed his family wealth among them, selected those who had served with merit and promoted them, and said, "You gentlemen, out of regard for our forebears, do not wish me to leave—this feeling is very deep.

sentences.zh: 然使承元違天子之詔，其罪大矣。

translations.literal: Yet if Chengyuan defies the Son of Heaven's decree, the crime would be grave indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if I defy the Son of Heaven's decree, the crime would be grave indeed.

sentences.zh: 昔李師道之未敗也，朝廷嘗赦其罪，師道欲行，諸將固留之。

translations.literal: In the past, before Li Shidao's defeat, the court once pardoned his crimes; Shidao wished to go, but the generals forcibly kept him.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, before Li Shidao's defeat, the court once pardoned his crimes; Shidao wished to go, but the generals forcibly kept him.

sentences.zh: 其後殺師道者亦諸將也。

translations.literal: Those who later killed Shidao were also the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Those who later killed Shidao were also the generals.

sentences.zh: 諸將勿使承元為師道，則幸矣。」

translations.literal: If you gentlemen do not make Chengyuan into another Shidao, that would be fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not make me into another Shidao, that would be fortunate."

sentences.zh: 因涕泣不自勝，且拜之。

translations.literal: He wept uncontrollably and bowed to them as he spoke.
translations.idiomatic: He wept uncontrollably as he spoke and bowed to them.

sentences.zh: 十將李寂等十餘人固留承元，承元斬以徇，軍中乃定。

translations.literal: More than ten officers including Colonel Li Ji forcibly tried to keep Chengyuan; Chengyuan had them executed as a warning, and only then was the army stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten officers including Colonel Li Ji forcibly tried to keep Chengyuan; Chengyuan had them executed as a warning, and only then was the army stabilized.

sentences.zh: 丁未，承元赴滑州。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Chengyuan departed for Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Chengyuan departed for Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 將吏或以鎮州器用財貨行，承元悉命留之。

translations.literal: Officers and clerks wished to take along Zhenzhou's utensils and goods; Chengyuan ordered all of it left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and clerks wished to take Zhenzhou's utensils and goods with them; Chengyuan ordered everything left behind.

sentences.zh: 上將幸華清宮，戊午，宰相率兩省供奉官詣延英門，三上表世諫，且言：「如此，臣輩當扈從。」

translations.literal: The emperor was about to visit Huaqing Palace; on wuwu, the chief ministers led the two secretariats' attendants to the Yanying Gate, thrice submitting memorials of urgent remonstrance, adding: "If it must be so, then we your servants must accompany you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to visit Huaqing Palace; on wuwu, the chief ministers led the two secretariats' attendants to the Yanying Gate, thrice submitting urgent remonstrances, adding, "If it must be so, then we your servants must accompany you."

sentences.zh: 求面對，皆不聽。

translations.literal: They sought a face-to-face audience; none was granted.
translations.idiomatic: They asked for an audience; the emperor refused to hear them.

sentences.zh: 諫官伏門下，至暮，乃退。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials prostrated themselves at the gate; only at dusk did they withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials lay prostrate at the gate and did not withdraw until evening.

sentences.zh: 己未，未明，上自復道出城，幸華清宮，獨公主、駙馬、中尉、神策六軍使帥禁兵千餘人扈從，晡時還宮。

translations.literal: On jiwei, before dawn, the emperor left the city by the Fudao and visited Huaqing Palace, accompanied only by princesses, imperial sons-in-law, the chief eunuch, the six Shence Army commanders, and a little over a thousand palace guards; he returned to the palace at the hour of shen.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, before dawn, the emperor left the city by the secret pass and went to Huaqing Palace, accompanied only by princesses, imperial sons-in-law, the chief eunuch, the six Shence Army commanders, and a little over a thousand palace guards; he returned to the palace in the afternoon.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己已朔，鹽州奏：吐蕃千餘人圍烏、白池。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day of jisi, Yanchou reported: over a thousand Tibetans besieged the Wu and Bai pools.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the first day of jisi, Yanchou reported that more than a thousand Tibetans were besieging the Wu and Bai pools.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，西川奏南詔二萬人入界，請討吐蕃。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Xichuan reported that twenty thousand Nanzhao troops had entered the border and requested permission to attack Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Xichuan reported that twenty thousand Nanzhao troops had crossed the border and asked to campaign against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 癸未，容管奏破黃少卿萬餘眾，拔營柵三十六。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Rongguan reported crushing Huang Shaoqing's forces of over ten thousand and capturing thirty-six stockades.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Rongguan reported defeating Huang Shaoqing's force of more than ten thousand and taking thirty-six stockades.

sentences.zh: 時少卿久未平，國子祭酒韓愈上言：「臣去年貶嶺外，熟知黃家賊事。

translations.literal: Huang Shaoqing had long gone undefeated; Han Yu, Director of the Directorate of Education, submitted a memorial: "Last year I was banished to the Lingnan region and came to know the affairs of the Huang bandits well.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shaoqing had long remained undefeated; Han Yu, Director of the Directorate of Education, submitted a memorial: "Last year I was banished to the south and came to know the Huang bandits well.

sentences.zh: 其賊無城郭可居，依山傍險，自稱洞主，尋常亦各營生，急則屯聚相保。

translations.literal: These bandits have no walled towns to live in; they rely on mountains and rivers for safety, call themselves cave chiefs, ordinarily each make their own living, and when pressed gather together for mutual protection.
translations.idiomatic: They have no walled towns to live in; they cling to mountains and rivers, call themselves cave chiefs, ordinarily make their own living, and when pressed gather together for mutual protection.

sentences.zh: 比緣邕管經略使多不得人，德既不能綏懷，威又不能臨制，侵欺虜縛，以致怨恨。

translations.literal: Recently because the military commissioners of Yong and Rong circuits often were unsuitable men, their virtue could not pacify the people nor their authority restrain them—they mistreated and bound the natives, provoking resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the military commissioners of Yong and Rong circuits have too often been the wrong men: lacking virtue to win people over and authority to keep them in check, they mistreated and bound the natives until resentment boiled over.

sentences.zh: 遂攻劫州縣，侵暴平人，或復私仇，或貪小利，或聚或散，終亦不能為事。

translations.literal: Thus they raided prefectures and counties, harmed common people, sometimes to settle private grudges, sometimes for small profit; they might gather or scatter, but in the end could accomplish nothing of lasting consequence.
translations.idiomatic: So they raided prefectures and counties and preyed on common people—sometimes to settle private scores, sometimes for petty gain; they might gather or scatter, but in the end could accomplish nothing lasting.

sentences.zh: 近者征討本起裴行立、陽旻，此兩人者本無遠慮深謀，意在邀功求賞。

translations.literal: The recent punitive campaigns began with Pei Xingli and Yang Min—neither had far-sighted plans, both meant only to claim merit and seek rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The recent campaigns began with Pei Xingli and Yang Min—men without far-sighted plans who sought only glory and reward.

sentences.zh: 亦緣見賊未屯聚之時，將謂單弱，爭獻謀計。

translations.literal: Also because when the bandits had not yet gathered, they were thought weak, and many vied to offer stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Also, when the bandits had not yet massed, everyone took them for easy prey and vied to offer plans.

sentences.zh: 自用兵以來，已經二年，前後所奏殺獲計不下二萬餘人，倘皆非虛，賊已尋盡。

translations.literal: Since troops were committed, two years have passed; successive reports of enemies killed or captured total no less than twenty thousand—if none were false, the bandits would already be gone.
translations.idiomatic: Two years of campaigning have produced reports of more than twenty thousand killed or captured; if none of those figures were false, the bandits would already be gone.

sentences.zh: 至今賊猶依舊，足明欺罔朝廷。

translations.literal: Yet the bandits remain as before—enough to show the court has been deceived.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the bandits remain as before—enough to show the court has been deceived.

sentences.zh: 邕、容兩管，經此凋弊，殺傷疾疫，十室九空，如此不已，臣恐嶺南一道未有寧息之時。

translations.literal: The Yong and Rong circuits have been devastated by this: casualties, pestilence—nine houses in ten stand empty. If this continues, I fear Lingnan will never know peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Rong circuits have been devastated—casualties, pestilence, nine houses in ten standing empty. If this goes on, I fear Lingnan will never know peace.

sentences.zh: 自南討已來，賊徒亦甚傷損，察其情理，厭苦必深。

translations.literal: Since the southern campaign began, the bandits too have suffered heavy losses; judging their mood, their weariness and bitterness must run deep.
translations.idiomatic: Since the southern campaign began, the bandits too have suffered heavily; judging their mood, their weariness and bitterness must run deep.

sentences.zh: 賊所處荒僻，假如盡殺其人，盡得其地，在於國計不為有益。

translations.literal: The bandits' territory is remote and barren; even if every one were killed and every inch of land taken, it would benefit the state not at all.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory is remote and barren; even if every bandit were killed and every inch of land taken, the state would gain nothing from it.

sentences.zh: 若因改元大慶，赦其罪戾，遣使宣諭，必望風降伏。

translations.literal: If, taking advantage of the great celebration of the new reign era, their crimes were pardoned and envoys sent to proclaim amnesty, they would surely surrender at the first word.
translations.idiomatic: If, amid the great celebration of the new reign era, their crimes were pardoned and envoys sent to proclaim amnesty, they would surely surrender at the first word.

sentences.zh: 仍為選擇有威信者為經略使，苟處置得宜，自然永無侵叛之事。」

translations.literal: Moreover, choose a man of proven authority as military commissioner; if matters are handled properly, raids and rebellion will naturally cease forever."
translations.idiomatic: Choose as military commissioner a man of proven authority; handle matters properly, and raids and rebellion will naturally cease forever."

sentences.zh: 上不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor did not adopt his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not adopt his advice.

sentences.zh: 憲宗昭文章武大聖至神孝皇帝下長慶元年（

translations.literal: Below: Emperor Xianzong, the Filial Emperor of Great Culture, Martial Prowess, Sagely Sagacity, and Divine Spirit — Year 1 of Changqing (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong — Year 1 of Changqing (

sentences.zh: 辛丑，公元八二一年）

translations.literal: xinchou, AD 821)
translations.idiomatic: xinchou, AD 821)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛丑，上祀圓丘。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinchou, the emperor sacrificed at the Circular Mound Altar.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinchou, the emperor sacrificed at the Circular Mound Altar.

sentences.zh: 赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign era.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign era.

sentences.zh: 河北諸道各令均定兩稅。

translations.literal: All circuits of Hebei were ordered to equalize and fix the two-tax system.
translations.idiomatic: All circuits of Hebei were ordered to equalize and fix the two-tax system.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎、同平章事蕭俛，介潔疾惡，為相，重惜官職，少所引拔。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Chancellery and co-equal chief minister Xiao Mian was upright, scrupulous, and hated evil; as chief minister he set great store by official posts and rarely promoted anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Chancellery and co-equal chief minister Xiao Mian was upright, scrupulous, and hated evil; as chief minister he set great store by office and rarely promoted anyone.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使王播大修貢奉，且以賂結宦官，求為相，段文昌復左右之。

translations.literal: Xichuan military commissioner Wang Bo greatly increased tribute and also bribed eunuchs to seek the chancellorship; Duan Wenchang again supported him from the side.
translations.idiomatic: Xichuan military commissioner Wang Bo greatly increased tribute and bribed eunuchs to win the chancellorship; Duan Wenchang again backed him.

sentences.zh: 詔征播詣京師。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Bo to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Bo to the capital.

sentences.zh: 俛屢於延英力爭，言：「播纖邪，物論沸騰，不可以污台司。」

translations.literal: Mian repeatedly argued strenuously at Yanying Hall, saying: "Bo is petty and unscrupulous; public opinion seethes—he must not stain the chief-ministerial office."
translations.idiomatic: Mian repeatedly argued strenuously at Yanying Hall, saying, "Bo is petty and unscrupulous; public opinion seethes—he must not stain the chief-ministerial office."

sentences.zh: 上不聽，俛遂辭位。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen, and Mian resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen, and Mian resigned.

sentences.zh: 己未，播至京師。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Bo arrived at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Bo arrived at the capital.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，俛罷為右僕射。

translations.literal: On renxu, Mian was removed and made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Mian was removed and made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俛固辭僕射，二月，癸酉，改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Mian firmly declined the vice directorship; in the second month, on guiyou, he was reassigned as Minister of the Ministry of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Mian firmly declined the vice directorship; in the second month, on guiyou, he was reassigned Minister of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 盧龍節度使劉總既殺其父兄，心常自疑，數見父兄為崇。

translations.literal: Lu-Long military commissioner Liu Zong, having killed his father and elder brothers, was often troubled in conscience and repeatedly saw his father and brothers as vengeful spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Lu-Long military commissioner Liu Zong, having killed his father and elder brothers, was haunted by guilt and repeatedly saw his father and brothers as vengeful spirits.

sentences.zh: 常於府捨飯僧數百，使晝夜為佛事，每視事退則處其中；

translations.literal: He regularly fed several hundred monks at his headquarters and had Buddhist rites performed day and night; whenever he finished handling affairs he withdrew into their midst;
translations.idiomatic: He regularly fed several hundred monks at headquarters and had Buddhist rites performed day and night; whenever he finished business he withdrew among them;

sentences.zh: 或處他室，則驚悸不能寐。

translations.literal: if he stayed in another room, he would start awake and unable to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: if he stayed in another room, he would start awake and unable to sleep.

sentences.zh: 晚年，恐懼尤甚。

translations.literal: In his later years his fear grew especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years his fear grew especially severe.

sentences.zh: 亦見河南、北皆從化，己卯，奏乞棄官為僧。

translations.literal: He also saw that both Henan and Hebei had submitted; on jimao he memorialized asking to abandon office and become a monk.
translations.idiomatic: He also saw that both Henan and Hebei had submitted; on jimao he memorialized asking to abandon office and become a monk.

sentences.zh: 仍乞賜錢百萬緡以賞將士。

translations.literal: He also asked that a million strings of cash be granted to reward his troops.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that a million strings of cash be granted to reward his troops.

sentences.zh: 上面諭西川節度使王播令歸鎮，播累表乞留京師。

translations.literal: The emperor had instructed Xichuan military commissioner Wang Bo to return to his post; Bo repeatedly memorialized asking to remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had instructed Xichuan military commissioner Wang Bo to return to his post; Bo repeatedly memorialized asking to remain in the capital.

sentences.zh: 會中書侍郎、同平章事段文昌請退，壬申，以文昌同平章事；

translations.literal: When Vice Director of the Secretariat and co-equal chief minister Duan Wenchang requested to retire, on renshen Wenchang was made co-equal chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Director of the Secretariat and co-equal chief minister Duan Wenchang asked to retire, on renshen Wenchang was made co-equal chief minister;

sentences.zh: 充西州節度使；

translations.literal: and appointed military commissioner of Xizhou;
translations.idiomatic: and appointed military commissioner of Xichuan;

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士杜元穎為戶部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Du Yuanying was made Vice Minister of Revenue and co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Du Yuanying was made Vice Minister of Revenue and co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 以播為刑部尚書，充鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Bo was made Minister of Justice and Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was made Minister of Justice and Salt and Iron Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元穎，淹之六世孫也。

translations.literal: Yuanying was the sixth-generation descendant of Du Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying was the sixth-generation descendant of Du Yan.

sentences.zh: 回鶻保義可汗卒。

translations.literal: The Uyghur Baoyi Khan died.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur Baoyi Khan died.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸丑，以劉總兼侍中，充天平節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month, on guichou, Liu Zong was additionally made Palace Attendant and appointed military commissioner of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guichou, Liu Zong was additionally made Palace Attendant and appointed military commissioner of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 以宣武節度使張弘靖為盧龍節度使。

translations.literal: Xuanwu military commissioner Zhang Hongjing was made Lu-Long military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu military commissioner Zhang Hongjing was made Lu-Long military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以權知京兆尹盧士玫為瀛莫觀察使。

translations.literal: On yimao, Acting Metropolitan Governor Lu Shimei was made overseer of Ying and Mo.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Acting Metropolitan Governor Lu Shimei was made overseer of Ying and Mo.

sentences.zh: 丁已，詔劉總兄弟子侄皆除官，大將僚佐亦宜超擢，百姓給復一年，軍士賜錢一百萬緡。

translations.literal: On dingsi, an edict appointed all of Liu Zong's brothers, sons, and nephews to office, ordered that senior generals and staff also be promoted, granted the common people a one-year tax exemption, and bestowed a million strings of cash on the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, an edict appointed all of Liu Zong's brothers, sons, and nephews to office, ordered senior generals and staff promoted as well, granted the people a one-year tax exemption, and bestowed a million strings of cash on the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 戊午，立皇弟憬為鄜王，悅為瓊王，惸為沔王，懌為婺王，愔為茂王，怡為光王，協為淄王，憺為衢王，惋為澶王；

translations.literal: On wuwu, the emperor's younger brothers Jing, Yue, Qiong, Yi, Yin, Yi, Xie, Tan, and Wan were enfeoffed as Princes of Fu, Qiong, Mian, Wu, Mao, Guang, Zi, Qu, and Chan respectively;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the emperor's younger brothers Jing, Yue, Qiong, Yi, Yin, Yi, Xie, Tan, and Wan were enfeoffed as Princes of Fu, Qiong, Mian, Wu, Mao, Guang, Zi, Qu, and Chan respectively;

sentences.zh: 皇子湛為景王，涵為江王，湊為漳王，溶為安王，瀍為穎王。

translations.literal: the imperial sons Zhan, Han, Cou, Rong, and Chan were enfeoffed as Princes of Jing, Jiang, Zhang, An, and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: the imperial sons Zhan, Han, Cou, Rong, and Chan were enfeoffed as Princes of Jing, Jiang, Zhang, An, and Ying.

sentences.zh: 劉總奏懇乞為僧，且以其私第為佛寺。

translations.literal: Liu Zong memorialized earnestly asking to become a monk and to convert his private residence into a Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zong earnestly memorialized asking to become a monk and to convert his private residence into a Buddhist temple.

sentences.zh: 詔賜總名大覺，寺名報恩，遣中使以紫僧服及天平節鉞、侍中告身並賜之，惟其所擇。

translations.literal: An edict granted Zong the monastic name Dajue and the temple the name Bao'en; an imperial envoy was sent bearing purple monastic robes together with the Tianping command baton and Palace Attendant commission, all to be given at his choice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Zong the monastic name Dajue and the temple the name Bao'en; an imperial envoy was sent with purple monastic robes, the Tianping command baton, and a Palace Attendant commission for him to take as he chose.

sentences.zh: 詔未至，總已削髮為僧，將士欲遮留之，總殺其唱帥者十餘人，夜，以印節授留後張玘，遁去。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrived, Zong had already tonsured himself and become a monk; when officers and soldiers tried to detain him, Zong killed more than ten ringleaders; that night he handed the seal and command baton to acting commissioner Zhang Qi and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrived, Zong had already tonsured himself; when officers and soldiers tried to detain him, he killed more than ten ringleaders, and that night handed the seal and command baton to acting commissioner Zhang Qi and fled.

sentences.zh: 及明，軍中始知之。

translations.literal: Only at dawn did the army learn of it.
translations.idiomatic: Only at dawn did the army learn of it.

sentences.zh: 玘奏總不知所在。

translations.literal: Qi reported that Zong's whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Qi reported that Zong's whereabouts were unknown.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，卒於定州之境。

translations.literal: On guihai, he died within the borders of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, he died within the borders of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士李德裕，吉甫之子也，以中書舍人李宗閔嘗對策譏切其父，恨之。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Li Deyu, son of Li Jifu, bore a grudge because Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Zongmin had once in a policy examination mocked his father sharply.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Li Deyu, son of Li Jifu, bore a grudge because Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Zongmin had once mocked his father sharply in a policy examination.

sentences.zh: 宗閔又與翰林學士元稹爭進取有隙。

translations.literal: Zongmin also had a rift with Hanlin Academician Yuan Zhen over competing for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin also feuded with Hanlin Academician Yuan Zhen over competing for advancement.

sentences.zh: 右補闕楊汝士與禮部侍郎錢徽掌貢舉，西川節度使段文昌、翰林學士李紳各以書屬所善進士於徽；

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Officer Yang Rushi and Vice Minister of Rites Qian Hui oversaw the civil examinations; Xichuan military commissioner Duan Wenchang and Hanlin Academician Li Shen each wrote recommending favored candidates to Hui;
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance Officer Yang Rushi and Vice Minister of Rites Qian Hui oversaw the civil examinations; Xichuan military commissioner Duan Wenchang and Hanlin Academician Li Shen each wrote recommending favored candidates to Hui;

sentences.zh: 及榜出，文昌、紳所屬皆不預焉，及第者，鄭朗，覃之弟；

translations.literal: when the list was posted, none of those recommended by Wenchang or Shen passed; those who passed included Zheng Lang, younger brother of Tan;
translations.idiomatic: when the list was posted, none of those recommended by Wenchang or Shen had passed; among those who passed was Zheng Lang, Tan's younger brother;

sentences.zh: 裴譔，度之子；

translations.literal: Pei Zan, son of Du;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zan, son of Pei Du;

sentences.zh: 蘇巢，宗閔之婿；

translations.literal: Su Chao, Zongmin's son-in-law;
translations.idiomatic: Su Chao, Zongmin's son-in-law;

sentences.zh: 楊殷士，汝士之弟也。

translations.literal: Yang Yinshi was Rushi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yinshi was Rushi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 文昌言於上曰：「今歲禮部殊不公，所取進士皆子弟無藝，以關節得之。」

translations.literal: Wenchang said to the emperor: "This year's Ministry of Rites was grossly unfair; the jinshi chosen were all sons and relatives without talent, who gained admission through connections."
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang told the emperor, "This year's Ministry of Rites was grossly unfair; the jinshi chosen were all sons and relatives without talent who gained admission through connections."

sentences.zh: 上以問諸學士，德裕、稹、紳皆曰：「誠如文昌言。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the academicians; Deyu, Zhen, and Shen all said: "It is indeed as Wenchang says."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the academicians; Deyu, Zhen, and Shen all said, "It is indeed as Wenchang says."

sentences.zh: 上乃命中書舍人王起等覆試。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Qi and others to re-examine them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Qi and others to re-examine them.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁丑，詔黜朗等十人，貶徽江州刺史，宗閔劍州刺史，汝士開江令。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingchou, an edict stripped ten men including Lang of their degrees; Hui was demoted to prefect of Jiangzhou, Zongmin to prefect of Jianzhou, and Rushi to magistrate of Kaijiang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingchou, an edict stripped ten men including Lang of their degrees; Hui was demoted to prefect of Jiangzhou, Zongmin to prefect of Jianzhou, and Rushi to magistrate of Kaijiang.

sentences.zh: 或勸徽奏文昌、紳屬書，上必悟。

translations.literal: Some urged Hui to memorialize submitting Wenchang's and Shen's recommendation letters—the emperor would surely understand.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Hui to memorialize submitting Wenchang's and Shen's recommendation letters—the emperor would surely see the truth.

sentences.zh: 徽曰：「苟元愧心，得喪一致，奈何奏人私書，豈士君子所為邪！」

translations.literal: Hui said: "If my conscience is clear, gain and loss are the same—how could I memorialize another man's private letters? Is that what a gentleman would do?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "If my conscience is clear, gain and loss are the same—how could I memorialize another man's private letters? Is that what a gentleman would do?"

sentences.zh: 取而焚之，時人多之。

translations.literal: He took the letters and burned them; people at the time widely praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He took the letters and burned them; people at the time widely praised him.

sentences.zh: 紳，敬玄之曾孫；

translations.literal: Shen was the great-grandson of Li Jingxuan;
translations.idiomatic: Shen was the great-grandson of Li Jingxuan;

sentences.zh: 起，播之弟也。

translations.literal: Qi was Bo's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was Bo's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 自是德裕、宗閔各分朋黨，更相傾軋，垂四十年。
